review_text: I purchased this laptop on the 18th and today is the 24th. I have read a lot of reviews complaining about heating issues and yes they are right. This laptop is a heater. It will be very helpful during the winter season.But I am keeping this as I have liked it and that's why the good 3 stars I am giving.When you use any laptop for the first few days, it heats up pretty badly because of a lot of updates going on in the background. I was almost scared when I see it heats up super bad and was thinking to return it. But that was just one time. But still, it heats up more than a normal laptop should. I didn't expect it because it is an i3 12th gen and has an underpowered processor.If you want to use this laptop, you will need a laptop cooler and it will be ok.Why I am not returning it?I like it, it looks very beautiful and light and has a nice display and it can handle my coding work. I just purchased it as a backup laptop because my main laptop Asus Vivobook runs 14 to 18hrs a day for the last 5 yrs and it needs some rest.Personally, I won't recommend this laptop. Maybe try Asus or HP. Asus gives the same features with a crap display and powerful i3 processor at a cheaper price.Here in short :-PROS -1) Compact and lightweight2) Good Display and sound3) Doesn't hang. Actually, it will depend on you. I will need to increase RAM to 16gb because I have heavy software and it this i3 can handle it, just need more ram. For Personal usage, it is great.CONS -1) Heating Issues like everyone mentioned. I am just not returning it as it is ok for me.2) Severe Touchpad Issue.EDIT - 14th May, 2023Severe Touchpad Issue. Many times I am clicking touchpad which should trigger left click like all laptops do but sometimes it acts weird and trigger right click. Then it becomes worst and then touchpad stops working. It has happened like 4 times already. It is a brand new laptop and not even 1 month and such a major issue. I reset my laptop. I thought it is because I am using same account of old laptop. In new account on fresh installation, same issue 2 times already. I am disabling this touchpad and using mouse now. I will throw it to the service center in few days.EDIT - 9th July, 20231) Laptop is working fine but touchpad and mouse issue still. I am still using my 6yrs old laptop as my main laptop because its mousepad is fine and better that this laptop. I tested 3 different mouse and it is not smooth but those mouses work fine in old laptop and other laptops too. So something software related issue i guess. I am writing typing from this DELL laptop. I am shutting it down because I cant work fast due to random touchpad issue, will resume work from old laptop. Looks like I have wasted my 40k. May be I will sell this laptop here in Manila, PH and buy some other laptop from here. No more Online laptop now. Next laptop will test fully by using it for 5-10 minutes. Still not recommending this laptop. My coding work is very very light. Even 10 yrs old 2nd generation I3 processor can handle it. So it is not a coding issue.Edit: 31st January, 2024Laptop is working fine for last 3-4 months and no issue now. Specially no touchpad issue. I guess it was software issue. So I am increasing Ratings from 2 to 4 now. Won't still give 5 stars though because of earlier issue. Now this laptop is my main laptop and I use it daily. I bought it as a backup laptop though. Will update after 4-5 months of usage and re-write proper review after 1 year of usageEdit: 21st August 2024.Well, on 14th August, 2024, laptop stopped working. I sent it to Dell repair and found motherboard is dead. They need to replace it whole.So I am not recommending this laptop. People say right. Never bought expensive stuffs online. This is 4th laptop and 1st online and so huge issue. Motherboard estimation is 16500 right now. Luckily I have insurance, I am not sure how much will they cover. My Asus, HP, Compaq and Macbook never got motherboard issue and all lasted long. This one gave so big issues even from start and now look at it.

review_title: Good value, but watch for damage and who you buy from!
review_text: Good value. I purchased this model: (HP 255 G10 Laptop, Ryzen 3 7330U, 15.6", 16GB RAM, 1TB SSD with Windows 11 Pro) from the seller Chromebook Prosale via Amazon for $399 in December of 2024.I had to return the first one because it had a RAM error. Every other time I started it, the Caps Lock LED would blink (3 long and two short). According to the documentation, that meant a RAM issue. Might have just needed a cleaning or the RAM was installed improperly. (more on that later.) I'll never know because I didn't want to void the warranty. So I sent it back and the seller promptly sent a new one. No errors on that one. YAY!Booted it up and it indeed had no errors, recognized all hardware, and had Windows 11 Pro installed. All good. Pretty quick. WiFi has typical range. There are two USB ports, one HDMI port, and one 1/8" audio jack. Battery holds a charge like a champ. No security port. However, I'm pretty satisfied with this laptop.Being satisfied, I then voided the warranty and opened the system to take a look. (I don't recommend this for the casual user because, though I'm not sure, I think it will void your warranty - if they find out that is!)Now the interesting part:TLDR: Be careful when buying from third-party sellers. You might save money, but you never know where the laptop has been or whose grubby paws were inside it!See attached image of the RAM. Note that only one stick is covered with a sticker. This leads me to believe that HP built this laptop with 8 GB of RAM (1 stick) originally. I can't prove it, but I think that the seller (or another intermediary) installed the 2nd stick of RAM to bring it up to 16 GB. Three clues led me to this deduction (which is guesswork): 1 - the lack of a sticker. That's weak sauce, and HP QA would probably not let that pass before leaving the manufacturer. 2. One of the panel's front corners was slightly lifted off two of the clips, as if the person who closed the panel (after installing the RAM) didn't finish the job properly. Made it easier for me to pop the panel though! 3. The first laptop I received had that RAM issue I mentioned. That would probably not pass QA at an HP manufacturing plant either. Standard procedure is to have a system booted at least three times.Am I happy with my assumption? No. But I'll deal with it after inspecting the RAM installed and comparing it with the first 8 GB stick. The laptop looks clean and I inspected Windows 11 as well for any "weirdness" or inappropriate programs.That said, would I purchase this again or recommend it. Only if a person's sole criteria for buying was price. Generally, I recommend buying laptops from the manufacturer directly.

review_title: Cheap laptop but be careful of variations
review_text: This is a low-spec laptop at a similarly matching budget price but be careful if you buy one of the higher specs (more than 16GB of memory and 512GB of storage). Those aren't available OEM configurations and the seller may have upgraded the laptop after market with generic (non-OEM) components. For example, the listing may be for an AMD Ryzen 3 7330U processor but what's actually received is a Intel Core i3-N305. Besides the, non-HP memory upgrade and SSD upgrade, it's also a bait and switch of the CPU that's $270 less for the Intel CPU if you look at standalone pricing on Amazon. Be careful to check the box and equipment you received, especially if it has stickers on it, that seem to match what you ordered but not quite.

review_title: IMHO good choice for a basic gaming laptop
review_text: Adequate laptop for gaming. It can run most games that are playable from Steam (non streaming 2025). I've played No Man's Sky, Lightyear Frontier, Towers of Agasbah, Palworld, Starfield and others of that caliber. I stream XBOX game pass with no hiccups and it connects to Microsoft Games.Three cons: battery life, loud fan and Microsoft. All aforementioned are self explained. Microsoft software/ bloatware took what can be a great laptop experience and ruined it. It needs to be updated out the box and it continues to update even when you disable auto update. Their 2 step authentication is mentally draining and time consuming for no reason. The software NEVER remembers your information so you have to constantly log in even after short term use. DO NOT ALLOW FOR PIN LOG IN. I learned this from my other Microsoft based laptop. It will log you out every time you close and will claim your password is invalid. If you're not using this for strictly entertainment and you need to lock your devices, this is not a good choice for a personal laptop.I put legs on this laptop because it gets extremely hot. It has never cut off for over heating but I do keep it on a cooling mat. The fan runs from the moment you turn it on. If you can't stand the fan running as background noise, this is not the laptop for you.I opted for the non touch screen version but the screen itself is good with great color saturation and no real glare. The backlit keyboard is a nice add on but I do not use it very often. The built in front facing camera is basic but keeps you from looking like you're streaming on a 2010 laptop. If you do plan on using this device for social media you may want to upgrade to an external camera.For the price point it's a good laptop for a casual to intermediate player. If you can get past the Microsoft harassment it could be a fine everyday PC. Laptop is made well and has some heft to it. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth work excellent and I have connected an Xbox controller with no issues.I'm on the fence about recommending as it has some quirks it has may annoy some. I bought it in anticipation for a new game possibly releasing in 2026. I'm hoping this won't be obsolete when it drops. There are better options but if your on a budget this is an ok device to get you started.

For users who frequently use the middle button—such as CAD professionals—this makes a noticeable difference. review_text: Ordered this controller and have used for more than 1 month now. So far I got to say this has to be the best controller I have ever used so far. Probably the best controller money can buy (In my opinion) I mainly use this controller for playing games on my PC and it works really well!! If you want read the entire review and if you don’t want to read the entire thing scroll down to the conclusion.Compatibility:I was first concerned whether it would work properly on PC as Sony Controllers usually don’t work properly on PC unless you use some 3rd party software. But, surprisingly I didn’t have to use any software it works out of the box well as long as game you’re playing has support for controller. All the games i own are on Steam and the awesome thing is, Steam has proper native support for a PS5 Controller so even if the game actually don’t support a PS5 Controller, Steam can force support it !!Haptics & Overall Experience:I got to say the haptics in this controller is the best and I prefer this much better to the Xbox Controllers. It is completely different to a regular controller as a regular one has only a rumble type vibration but Sony has used 2 haptic motors and gives you a phone type individual vibration feedbackAdaptive Triggers:Not all games have proper support to this feature but I got to test the adaptive triggers on Cyberpunk 2077 and in order for it to work you need to connect via a cable. But, the adaptive triggers is just mind blowing gives you a very realistic feeling & experience this is what mainly blew my mind.Battery Life:Takes some time to charge (around 4-5 hours I guess) but lasts really long so no need to worry about running out of battery in the middle of game definitely it has run for days after gaming daily on it.Build:Honestly speaking the build quality of the controller is really good and buttons and triggers have a good feedback and feel premium as well.Stick Drift or any Issues to be concerned of:So almost everyone’s who is planning to buy a controller will be concerned about this so called Stick Drift. One thing I’ll say is so far in my > 1 month of usage didn’t have any issues but there’s a way you can avoid it or be less worried of if you’re planning to buy one. Behind the controller there’s an FCC ID so when you buy one check behind the controller, if you’re FCC ID ends with a letter A or B or anything greater than that you’re all good to go and you’re controller will not get affected with stick drift easily. As Sony has updated their controllers some time back. But, if your controllers FCC ID ends with a number 1 then your controller is most likely to have some fault or issues so better to get it exchanged.Overall I have played games like Wukong, Cyberpunk, FortniteConclusion:Thank You! For reading my entire review if you did, then I would honestly recommend this controller to a PC player as well if you’re planning to buy one. Yes I know an Xbox Controller has better compatibility in Windows but Sony Controllers have the best experience in gaming.

review_text: Pathetic Fit and Finish – Not Worth the Premium PriceThe fit and finish are extremely disappointing, especially for a flagship product. I checked two units, and both had noticeable inconsistencies.Several buttons felt mushy, suggesting poor-quality membrane switches.The touchpad was misaligned, positioned slightly to the right instead of being properly centered.The left joystick produced a grinding noise, which raises serious concerns about quality control and long-term durability.The joysticks also didn't feel particularly smooth or precise for aiming compared to some third-party controllers.There is no Hall Effect technology, which is disappointing at this price point.The haptics and adaptive triggers are excellent, without any doubt. However, good features cannot completely compensate for poor fit and finish. These cosmetic and mechanical inconsistencies make me question the product's long-term reliability.For PC gaming, the experience is even more frustrating. The built-in speaker is practically useless, and there is no proper surround or simultaneous audio functionality. Audio is routed either through the controller or the PC, but not both in a convenient way. On top of that, a separate DSX purchase is required for better functionality, making the overall PC experience unnecessarily complicated and expensive.In my opinion, this controller should be priced at around ₹4,000 maximum. Paying significantly more is difficult to justify given the inconsistent build quality and limitations.Verdict: Not recommended for PC users. The excellent haptics and triggers are the only standout features, but the poor quality control, mushy buttons, joystick issues, lack of Hall Effect sticks, and additional software requirements make it hard to recommend at its current price.

review_text: prior to purchasing this specific trimmer i was using the prev gen philips 7000 trimmer (mg7715) and it worked perfectly for 3.5 years with no issues but unfortunately it fell out of my hand quite badly twice and the second fall killed it completely (right after the warranty expired) and thus i replaced it with this one without a second thought, the new one, right out of the box it feels lighter and the motor and blades are way more powerful, registered on the app and claimed the 5y extended warranty and im quite happy with that, if you’re confused btwn 5000 series and the 7000 series, go for this one if you want all the blades (but in my experience you only end up using 4-5 of the attachments at max), good thing about this trimmer is that all attachments from my mg7715 fit onto this one perfectly without any issues, charges full within 40 mins or so and the rapid charge feature gives you about 10 - 15 mins of usage after charging for 5-6 minsComing to the trimming part, i exclusively use this trimmer bcoz i get ingrown hair on my neck and jawline very easily after using a manual razor, however, this one delivers a close enough shave that is comparable to a stubble you’d possibly get the day after shaving you face clean with a manual razor and just like the prev gen there’s no ingrown hair or irritation at all and once you get the hang of it all the attachments work superbly,Also just something i noticed after using the prev gen for 3.5+ years, if you want your trimmer’s motor to function as good as new then try to avoid using this trimmer in the shower or getting its whole body wet, clean the blades and inside after every use and you’re done cleaning with water, dry well before putting it away and try to relube the blade attachment atleast once in 5-6 months for optimal performanceMy only gripe with the product is that even after so many years philips is still opting for its proprietary charging pin instead of type c charging which is something they could’ve adopted by now, or atleast they could’ve used a type c to proprietary charging pin instead of using a usb a port which making it albeit inconvenient, also at this price point they could’ve included a better storage pouch with a zip or a simple box instead of that flimsy pouch, but in all its a great product and you can buy blindly bcoz its philips

review_text: Its decent as a body trimmer but very bad as a beard trimmer.This model has multiple fixed sized combs in 2 mm increments and one special comb with 0.2 mm adjustability. The problem is, now one needs to carry all, or at least carry a 4-6 combs when traveling to maintain a fade. Previously I had a basic Philips BT3211 trimmer with a single adjustable comb from 1-10 mm so traveling with it was easy.The beard combs are also a bit sharp and the gap between the comb teeth too wide, and they don't pick up beard hairs on the side of face which are smaller.The nose trimmer doesn't do a good job at all. I have a basic Philips dedicated nose trimmer that does the job significantly better.The cable is USB on one end and a proprietary connector on the other end. Why can't they make it USB C on the trimmer side so you don't have to carry one extra cable + adapter? This is a very very poor design.Plus, the biggest problem, which I don't know how a company can be so stupid in 21st century - the trimmer only works on battery and you cannot operate it while on power. Sure, it has fast charging but come on, if a basic 1000 rupees Philips trimmer can work on both battery and power, there is no excuse why can't a 3k trimmer operate in the same way.Overall, I was much more satisfied by a cheap Philips trimmer than this fancy but stupid trimmer.The only advantage of this is that it is water resistant and can can be used in wet condition.I do not recommend people to buy this trimmer if they are buying it specifically for maintaining a beard.Very poorly designed product. Jack of some trades, master of none at all.

Although Philips claims IPx7 I do not recommend using it wet if longevity is desired, learning from my experience with the previous one. One thing i think causes the trimmer to get noisy and struggle over time is loss of lubrication. All blades come with a tinge of cream-like grease which is lost quickly. I think adding some silicone grease periodically will help maintain smooth like-new operation.

review_text: I recently got the Noise 3 Wireless On-Ear Headphones, and overall, I’m impressed. The sound quality is fantastic with rich bass and clear highs, thanks to the 40mm drivers. The low latency of up to 45ms is great for gaming or watching videos, ensuring no audio delay. With Bluetooth 5.3, the connection is stable and reliable, and the dual pairing feature is super convenient, allowing me to connect to two devices at once. The 70-hour playtime is incredible, meaning I don’t have to worry about charging often. However, the only downside is the comfort of the ear cushions. While they provide decent padding, they aren’t as comfortable as I had hoped, especially for long listening sessions. They could be softer and more cushioned to offer a better overall experience. Despite this, the sound quality and features make these headphones a great value for the price.

review_title: Premium Brand? My Noise Airwave Max 4 Didn't Even Last One Year
review_text: I purchased the Noise Airwave Max 4 headphones barely four months ago for my engineering college work and study sessions. They were used carefully, indoors, under completely normal conditions — no drops, no rough handling, no stretching, nothing careless whatsoever. Yet somehow, the headband has cracked from both sides within just a few months, making the headphones practically unusable.What makes this worse is that the product is STILL UNDER WARRANTY.Frankly, this level of durability is unacceptable for a product marketed as “premium.” A headphone designed for daily use should not structurally fail within a single college semester.When I reached out regarding the warranty claim (Ticket ID: 4379277), I was informed that this may be categorized as “physical damage” and therefore excluded from warranty coverage.And now, despite the product failing within the warranty period under normal usage, I am being asked to pay ₹1019 for repair.At this point, it honestly feels like the warranty exists only until a customer actually needs to use it.But let’s be realistic — when a product breaks during normal usage without any mishandling, that is not customer damage. That points toward poor material quality, weak structural design, or manufacturing failure. Calling every premature failure “physical damage” feels less like customer support and more like an easy escape from responsibility.Noise heavily markets durability, comfort, and reliability. However, those claims lose credibility when the product cannot withstand basic everyday use for even four months.As a customer, I did my part:• Used the headphones responsibly• Handled them carefully• Trusted the brand’s quality claimsUnfortunately, the product did not do its part.This raises a serious question:Does the Noise warranty actually protect customers from premature product failure?Or does the term “physical damage” simply become a blanket excuse to deny legitimate claims while customers are asked to pay for repairs even within warranty?Customers do not spend their money on “premium” products expecting them to become unusable within months. Durability is not a bonus feature — it is the bare minimum expectation.I genuinely hope Noise reviews this issue fairly and takes responsibility instead of dismissing it under technical wording. Because situations like this damage customer trust far more than the cost of honoring a genuine warranty claim.

Depending upon the codec the quality of your sound differs.This device seems to be defaulting to AAC (advcd audio encoding) which apple devices use. I had to go to "Developer Options" in android (to enable "Developer Options" in Android please google it) and try another codec. I switched to SBC (Sub-Band Codec) on my phone which is a very old codec and is prone to losses, and then it sounded fine. Attached two images for reference.for Samsung:1 Go to "Settings"2 Tap "About device" or "About phone"3 Tap “Software information”4 Tap “Build number” seven times. ...5 Enter your pattern, PIN or password to enable the Developer options menu.6 The "Developer options" menu will now appear in your Settings menu.PLEASE NOTE: YOUR PHONE NEEDS TO BE CONNECTED/PAIRED WITH THE HEADSET FOR YOU TO BE ABLE TO SEE THE BLUETOOTH CODEC OPTION IN YOUR "DEVELOPER OPTIONS" IN ANDROID. review_text: I’ve been using these earbuds from Diwali till today, and honestly, they’ve been FABULOUS. As a beginner audiophile, I can confidently say: just go for it. These deliver, and then some.🔄 Dual Device PairingWorks like a charm — fast, smooth, and without any issues.🔋 Battery BackupI use dual device pairing, dynamic EQ, AAC codec, and hi-res Apple Music.I get 5–6 hours of listening at 40–50% volume.Gaming: 3–5 hours (without ANC/transparency).Fast Charging: 5 minutes of charging gives ~40%, which lasts 1–2 hours.Full charge completes in around 15 minutes.The case lasts 1–2 days, depending on usage.⚠ Note: After around 1–2 months, my left earbud battery drains slightly faster than the right. Something to keep an eye on.🎧 Fit & ComfortLooks: Lavender version is stunning — looks premium.Fit:For normal use, fit is okay but not the most ergonomic.Left earbud fits ~90%, right fits perfectly. (Likely ear-shape dependent.)Not suitable for sleeping — feels uncomfortable.Light sweat can make them slip at times.🔇 ANC & TransparencyANC: Surprisingly good for the price. Cuts out around 98% of ambient noise, and with music feels like 100%.Transparency Mode: Very helpful while walking; natural and useful.For the price I paid (₹1699), this is a huge win.🎮 Gaming PerformanceDedicated game mode (~40ms).I play Valorant and felt zero lag.Spatial audio gives a wider soundstage — extremely helpful in competitive games.BGMI performance is also solid.🌀 Spatial AudioNoticeably good!If you prefer a wider and larger surround stage without echo, this one delivers beautifully.📶 ConnectivityRock-solid connection.Seamless switching between two devices (though you can’t play media on both at once).Easy reset process (hold both buds for 10+ seconds until beep, then put in case).No Dolby support on the earbuds, but my phone (Samsung F55) has it anyway, so no issues there.📞 Calling QualityClear, clean, and consistent.Mics are sensitive and provide good noise suppression.No issues whatsoever.✅ Overall VerdictAn extremely good product at this price point. 100% recommended.Buy it without hesitation — you’ll be more than satisfied.VALUE FOR MONEY

Jab aap jaldi mein ho aur connection na bane to irritate ho jaata hai insaan.🟡 5. Battery Backup – 3/5Battery backup thik-thak hai. 6-7 ghante single charge pe mil jaate hain aur case ke saath lagbhag 40 hours. Lekin jab earbuds use hi properly na ho to iska kya fayda?🔚 Final Verdict (6 Months Later):Shuruaat mein laga ki ₹1,000 ke andar badhiya deal hai, lekin 6 mahine ke andar hi lagne laga paisa barbaad kiya. Fit, sound, charging, aur connectivity – sab mein problems mili.Agar aap reliable aur long-lasting earbuds dhoond rahe ho, to thoda aur invest karna behtar hoga. Noise Buds Connect ko main personally recommend nahi karta.

review_text: I’ve been using it for more than 3 months, and it’s working fine. Here’s everything I’ve observed so far. Before this, I had a Noise Caliber, which was half the price of this one, so my comparison is based on that.Good FeaturesMic and Audio Quality: The mic and audio quality are good. While sitting behind someone riding a vehicle, I can clearly hear the voice from the watch during a call and talk to them comfortably.Water Resistance: The water resistance is good. I’ve had several "heart attack" moments with water, but the watch handled them well.Connecting Range: The connection range is good, and it stays connected well when in range.Bad FeaturesStep/Health Tracking: It’s not a good choice for someone who tracks steps or health information seriously. I have to reach for the button to check the time.Battery: The battery is fine. If not connected via Bluetooth, I only need to charge it once a week.App Features: I just realized the app doesn’t have a "find my watch" feature—come on, my Noise watch had this!Performance: It takes slightly longer to respond compared to my Noise watch.Display Quality: The icons and text look very low quality.Bluetooth Issues: When I turn on Bluetooth to connect with my OnePlus Nord CE 3 Lite and OnePlus Nord 3 buds, my phone connects to the buds first, then the watch. The watch somehow disconnects the voice from the buds, which is really annoying. I have to manually disconnect the watch to listen to audio on the buds.Other NotesRotating Dial: The rotating dial feature is good but doesn't have much use other than switching the home screen.Customization: The watch needs better customization options for the home screen.I hope this helps you decide if this watch is for you or not.

review_title: Painful to use, poor design, and disappointing support
review_text: I am extremely disappointed with my purchase of boAt Airdopes. I bought this product through Amazon, expecting at least basic comfort and usability. Unfortunately, the experience has been nothing short of terrible.The biggest issue is the faulty and uncomfortable design. Within just 5 minutes of wearing the earbuds, my ears start hurting badly—to the point that I have no option but to remove them. This is not a minor discomfort; it is actual pain. The earbuds have a hard lump immediately after the silicon tips (marked in red in the picture), which constantly presses against the ear cartilage. This design flaw makes prolonged use impossible and renders the product practically useless for listening to music, calls, or meetings.Earbuds are supposed to be ergonomic and comfortable. These are neither. If a product causes pain within minutes, it has fundamentally failed its purpose. No amount of sound quality or branding can compensate for something that physically hurts the user.To make matters worse, the after-sales experience was equally frustrating. When I contacted Amazon for a return, I was told that returns are not allowed, only a 10-day replacement, because that is boAt’s policy. This is extremely unfair when the issue is design-related and not something that can be “fixed” by replacing the same model. A replacement will still have the same painful design.So now I am stuck with a product that I cannot comfortably use and cannot return.In summary:❌ Painful to wear within minutes❌ Poor, non-ergonomic design❌ Hard lump near silicon tips hurts ear cartilage❌ Terrible customer experience❌ No proper return option for a defective designThis has been a waste of money. I would strongly advise potential buyers to stay away from this product, especially if you care about comfort or plan to use earbuds for more than a few minutes at a time. Also very disappointed with Amazon’s help desk for not standing by the customer in a genuine usability issue.Not recommended at all.

review_text: Great Mic for Calls, but Flawed Connectivity & Average Sound Quality​Price Paid: ₹999 (Freedom Sale 2026)Usage: ~1 Week​The Good​Mic Quality (The Standout Feature): Absolutely the best thing about these earbuds. Call quality is super clear, and the audio on the receiver’s end remains clean and crisp.​Fit & Passive Isolation: While there is no Active Noise Cancellation (ANC), the ergonomic fit sits securely in the ear and passively blocks out around 60% of ambient background noise.​The Average & Bad​Sound Quality: Below average to "okay" for ₹999. The audio feels muffled/blurred—there's minimal separation between vocals and instrumental tracks. It’s passable if you aren't an audiophile, but don't expect high detail.Spatial Mode: Nothing special or noteworthy. It feels like a gimmick that doesn't add any real depth or enhancement to the audio.​Noticeable Audio Latency: There is an annoying delay between the audio and video. Even while casually scrolling Reels or watching videos, the video runs visibly ahead of the sound you hear.​Build Quality: Feels cheap and lightweight. The case hinge is far too loose and pops open easily, even with a slight shake. literally feels like a ₹350 earpods the ones we get at Railway station.​The Frustrating (Connectivity Issues)​Faulty Dual Pairing: Switching between devices is a hassle. You often have to put the buds back into the case and pull them out again to switch connections.​Single Earbud Dropouts: Occasionally, one earbud stops outputting sound entirely, giving you a quick panic attack thinking it broke.​Auto-Connect Annoyance: If another previously paired device is nearby, the earbuds randomly prioritize it over your phone, leaving you struggling to get audio output. A dedicated touch control or physical button to toggle active devices is sorely missed.​Summary -​If your primary need is clear voice calls on a tight budget, these are worth ₹999. However, if you are buying these for music immersion, seamless multi-device switching, or a sturdy build, you might want to explore other options

review_text: The boAt Airdopes 141 Gen 2 continues to dominate the entry-level segment because it perfectly hits the sweet spot for budget conscious buyers who prioritize robust everyday performance over premium features. Reviewers consistently praise the upgraded ergonomic design of the stems, which provides a remarkably secure and fatigue-free seal during intense gym sessions or long daily commutes. The audio signature is undisputedly bass-forward, pumping out deep, energetic sub-bass frequencies that bring hip-hop and electronic music to life, though audiophiles note this tuning slightly muddies the mid-range vocals. Its standout feature remains the exceptional power management, offering a combined 48 hours of playback that keeps users away from wall chargers for days at a time. The inclusion of Type-C fast charging is a massive convenience, allowing you to salvage a dead battery with just a ten-minute quick top-up before heading out the door. For mobile gamers and video streaming enthusiasts, the dedicated BEAST™ Mode successfully drops latency low enough to eliminate annoying audio-to-video synchronization delays. However, the quad-microphone setup with ENx technology receives mixed feedback; while it isolates your voice beautifully inside a quiet bedroom or office, it noticeably struggles to suppress harsh ambient noises like heavy traffic or loud marketplace chatter. Additionally, while the touch controls are highly responsive, they can occasionally register accidental inputs when you are adjusting the earbuds in your ear. The overall build quality relies heavily on lightweight plastic, which keeps the case pocketable but leaves it prone to picking up micro-scratches over months of regular use. Despite minor flaws like the lack of a dedicated companion app for custom equalizer settings, its IPX4 sweat resistance and reliable Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity make it an incredibly dependable daily driver. Ultimately, it represents an unbeatable value proposition for anyone wanting maximum bass, long-lasting battery, and stable performance without breaking the bankThere should be black colour rubber buds

review_title: great product under low price range
review_text: Pros:1. The level of volume it gets to, is just awesome, it can get incredibly loud so if you're at the gym, these are perfect.2. Awesome Bass!3. Noise cancellation is just great, if you simply put them on without even any music playing, u won't be able to hear things around u very well, it's great for places like Gym.4. Lovely battery life, I've had them a week and only had to charge the case once, that too for just a few minutes. And the earbuds themselves, leave them in case for just five min and you'll be getting battery for a long long while.5. They are very comfortable, can be used for long periods of time.6. Affordable!7. The touch controls are very responsive, tap to pause, double tap right one for next song, double tap left one for either rewind or previous song. Can also pick up calls just by tapping.8. Multiple ear coverings are provided with it.9. Type C portCons:1. The sound quality is not bad or anything but it is slightly muffled as compared to good quality headphones etc. The bass is the highlight so it's great for music, but for movies or gaming, you won't get the most crisp audio.2. Some connectivity issues, sometimes i have to turn my Bluetooth on and off many times for it to work (this is occasional, not a daily or frequent occurrence) [Edit after 1 month use: it's now a very frequent issue]3. The mic quality is good if you are using your phone, but for some reason the quality is really bad if you are on PC4. Sometimes on WhatsApp, the mic will not be detected if you are on call with these earbuds, so you will end up having to take them off to accept a call sometimes. (Not an issue if you are the one dialing) i hope it's just a whatsapp issue rather than earbuds issue.Overall, I needed these for my gym since they play horrible music there (lol) so I'm very very happy with themHighly recommended for music and/or as a more affordable option as compared to JBL etc.

review_title: Great compact keyboard for daily use - with one miss
review_text: I was looking for a compact wireless keyboard, as I did not have much space on my table, and this one was the perfect fit for all my needs. I am using it across 2 laptops and the Bluetooth switch works perfect. The typing experience is great as it has really soft keys with very comfortable key height and spacing between the keys. I liked the fact that it has full sized arrow keys (most compact keyboards provide tiny up and down arrow keys). The function keys also work fine for my laptop and come in handy as I don't have to use my laptop keyboard for those.I wanted to have a black keyboard, but the white looks good and premium. I am getting adjusted to white colour.The only disappointment for me(and the reason for cutting down one star from my review) is the absence of a Home button. Being from a code development background, I use the Home and End buttons regularly to traverse text and code. The absence of a Home button is a huge struggle for me. I have been using this keyboard for over a month now, but still my fingers quite often search for the Home button. The menu button on the right side of the space bar is pretty useless for me, hope they had removed it and gave a Home button instead, or atleast gave me an option to configure a home button - that would have been super handy.Overall, it's a great compact keyboard for daily use. If you are fine without a Home button, I would definitely recommend this.

I didn't understand the logic behind omitting such a crucial button like "HOME" in a keyboard which is widely used during typing. I have used other TKL keyboards but haven't come across such an issue before. Some keyboards do have the "HOME" function under the FN option in TKL formats but still it remains available for users.To add to this, here are some points which can be implemented to make this keyboard even better:1. Type C charging which will do away with the AAA batteries.2. Multi-level adjustable front pegs which will make the typing experience much better3. A pro version of this keyboard with a bit premium price adding backlights which will enable usage even in low light scenarios.P.S. - I am not commenting on the battery life of this keyboard as of now as 24 hours is not at all a long enough usage window to evaluate battery backup. review_text: The media could not be loaded. I really wanted to love the Portronics Bubble Multimedia Wireless Keyboard. When I first got it, everything worked perfectly out of the box. I loved the noiseless keystrokes, and the dual connectivity (switching between the 2.4 GHz USB receiver and Bluetooth) was incredibly convenient for my setup.However, out of nowhere, the Windows key completely stopped working. It wasn't dropped, there were no spills, and it wasn't damaged in any way—it just suddenly died. The strangest part is that every single other key on the keyboard still works flawlessly. It is literally just the Windows key that has become completely unresponsive.I tried all the standard troubleshooting steps before writing this:Unplugged it and tried different USB ports, and switched to Bluetooth mode.Tested the keyboard on a completely different computer.Pressed Fn + P to ensure the keyboard was in Windows mode (and not accidentally set to Mac/iOS mode).Nothing worked. Since the Windows key is essential for how I navigate my PC and use shortcuts, having a dead key ruins the entire experience. It is incredibly frustrating for an otherwise great product to fail like this. Unless Portronics reaches out with a fix or replacement, I cannot recommend this keyboard.

I don't seem to notice any kind of change. Sure, It does help me moisturising my skin. However, apart from that I don't see any kind of change. I'm confused whether it's really affecting my pigmentation (for the better) or not. Whether it's making my skin healthy or not. I know it's only meant for moisturising the skin and not for any fairness treatment.For just moisturising the skin it's good. Apart from that, don't expect any kind of surprises from it. review_text: Solides Board auf der AM4 Plattform. Es ist natürlich sehr spärlich ausgestattet und ist selbst von Midrange noch ein gutes Stück entfernt. Aber ok, für den Einstieg ist es in Ordnung. Das A520M Prime ist wie alle Boards mit diesem Chipsatz lediglich PCI-E 3.0 fähig. Neuste Grafikkarten unterstützen ja bereits 5.0. Das Asus verfügt über 1x M.2 Slot für die SSD und 2x RAM Bänke, auch zu wenig für die heutige Zeit. SSDs können aber noch per Sata installiert werden. Die Mosfets liegen frei, ohne Kühlkörper. Ja klar, wenn man nen Ryzen 5600 und ne 2 TB SSD eingebaut hat, dazu noch nen 32 GB Kit ist man wahrscheinlich eh durch, mehr Aufrüsten würde ich nicht empfehlen. review_title: LIGHTWEIGHT AND HYDRATING, GOOD SUNPROTECTION TOO.
review_text: just received the product yesterday, writing my opinion after just first application. this is like a moisturizer, slightly runny creme like texture, easily gets absorbed in the skin, without leaving any oily residue and the best part no white cast what so ever. it blends in to the skin with minimal effort, almost immediately after application, settles in to non-greasy finish.now coming to the sunscreen filters, it has Butyl Methoxydibenzoylmethane (Avobenzone - the only globally available chemical sunscreen that gives proper UVA protection. It is not photostable so has to be combined with ingredients that help to stabilize it.), Terephthalylidene Dicamphor Sulfonic Acid (A L'Oréal-group exclusive sunscreen agent commonly called Mexoryl SX. As opposed to most sunscreen agents, it is water soluble and protects in the UVA range with a peak absorbance at 345 nm.), Phenylbenzimidazole Sulfonic Acid (A chemical sunscreen agent that gives a strong protection in the UVB (280-320nm) range with a peak protection at 306 nm.), Ethylhexyl Methoxycinnamate (Octinoxate - an old-school chemical sunscreen that absorbs UVB radiation (wavelengths: 280-320 nm). Not photostable and does not protect against UVA.), Ethylhexyl Salicylate (A colorless to light yellowish oily liquid that works as a UVB (280-320nm) sunscreen filter with a peak absorbance at 306 nm. It's not a strong filter in itself, it's always used in combination with other sunscreen agents.), Methylene Bis-Benzotriazolyl Tetramethylbutylphenol (Tinosorb M - a new generation, "hybrid" (between physical and chemical agents) sunscreen that gives broad-spectrum coverage and is highly photostable.). these combined modern and old school filters makes it a good and photo stable sunscreen.along with that it contains antioxidants like Niacinamide, Capsicum Annuum Fruit Extract, Tocopheryl Acetate to safeguard the skin from external pollutants, humectants like Glycerin and Sodium Hyaluronate for hydration, skin soothing agents like Blueberry Extract and Allantoin to calm down skin irritation. it also contains tapioca starch, which is known for absorbing oil, providing a matte finish, and creating a silky texture, so it is suitable for people with oily skin. it does not contain any fragrance, so less likely to irritate sensitive skin. I also did not feel any irritation or burning sensation in my eyes while application.the 125ml pack makes it economic also. 100% recommended for oily skin people.

review_title: Phenomenal Day 1 experience. Will review in a few months
review_text: My experience started on a Wednesday before Diwali on 23-Oct-2019 when my 2-year old Canon G1000 Ink tank printer just stopped printing and just spooled empty pages. Luckily I had purched OnsiteGo Extra Warranty. They responded asap and sent an engineer who couldnt fix it and decided to take it to their service center. Subsquent follow-ups confirmed that the printer couldnt be fixed and OnSiteGo refunded the entire invoice amount of Rs 7098 as Amazon gift vouchers by 30-Oct-2019. Not bad for a Rs 450 extended warranty.I wanted to go for a simple inktank printer and while i wanted to go wireless, there are no printers with just wireless. You have to buy it as a Multifunction which to me is fairly useless as I do a significant amount of scanning using Turboscan including legal documents, bills etc, and so waste of money. I did read a bit of literature on how to enable a non-wireless printer on a wifi network if the router had a usb port and voila my router (supplied by Airtel) which was a Huawei Hg4185 had one. So before i decided, i did a test with a neighbour's old epson Tx121 printer and it seemed to work. Secondly the cost of a good wireless inktank multi was almost twice the cost of a basic ink tank print only device. My choices narroed down to Canon G1010, Epson L130 and HP115,. all of which were single function, ink tank printers with no wireless and no duplex (which are the main add-on features as far as i was concerned).As i had previouly used Canon and HP in the past, looking at the reviews especially by one the gentlemen on Amazon who confirmed the wirless part, I decided to go ahead with the Epson L130. I ordered the same on Amazon on 30-Oct-2019 @ 17:00. The printer arrived prompty at 31-Oct-2019 @ 10:30. I called up Epson customer care @ 11:00 to log an installation request. I got a call from their installation at 12:00 and he landed at home by about 13:00 and by 14:00, we were all set. The printer defiitely looks sleek and doesnt need a lot of space. The only eye-sore is that the ink tanks are outside the core printer and is a little bit of nuisance but no ways a deal breaker.My wifi gig however did not work. After a lit bit of hair scratching, I disconnected the printer from the wifi router, shut down the router, connected back the printer and restarted the router. And bingo, the printer was available on the wifi network. You just need to make sure that the Epson L130 driver (either through the CD or online from the epson site) is installed on your computer. I think did the same on my dad's laptop and worked like a charm.The next step was to set it up for printing from a mobile device. We are thankfully an android household and once i followed the instructions on the google support site on Google cloud print, I was able to print from my android phone. Further you can also grant permission to others through email and as long as your printer is on and your wifi network is connected to the internet, you can print from anywhere in the world through your mobile. Quite cool indeed.SO overall, this is like any other inktank printer1/ Uses inktank technology (naturally) and prints decent prints at a cheap rate2/ Is slow (especially on color prints)3/ Doesnt make too much noise4/ Has just 2 buttons one for power and the other for indicating if there is an isssue (nothing comp;licated)5/ You will have to print at least a couple of prints a week to make sure that the nozzles are fine and that the ink doesnt go dry6/ I am expecting to see with lines in a few months (courtesy my canon G1000 experience) which will require a bit of nozzle cleaning.7/ very compact for a home office (more compact and ligher than my earlier Canon G1000)8/ Overall a good buy for home usage and which will hopefully last for the next 4-5 years with decent mainteance.So for a first day experience, am very happy. And lasly i did get the OnsiteGo extended warranty for 2 years. Hopefully their customer service continues at the same level as today.I will post a detailed update in a few months after testing it extensively. For now, totally blown away with both Amazon and Epson customer service and of course the printer

category: Computers & Accessories > Printers, Inks & Accessories > Printers > Inkjet Printers
review_title: THE BEST SINGLE-FUNCTION PRINTER FOR YOUR WIN AND MAC, WITH “OPTION” TO CONNECT WIRELESS AND CLOUD
review_text: REVIEW AFTER 6 MONTHS OF USE: Oh this printer is stupendous!!! It deserves an 8 star!!!I printed a photo last week (on Epson gloss paper) and it came 100% studio quality. Well, thats enough for me! I can now make posters at home, without spending extra bucks in a studio. Love it. buy it!!----------------------Let me first say, that the 5-star rating I have given is not because L130 is the best feature-packed printer in the market, but rather it was the “exact” printer I wanted per my technical requirement, specification, and budget---after a 2 month research.I am going to give a very detailed review, with some myth-busters. Yes, I see a lot of wrong Q&As and reviews that I would like to bust with my honest review on day-3 of my purchase.Home use, not for bulk or fast printing–This printer is a pure home or small business/shop use. Do not expect paper capacity beyond 40-50 (75 GSM) in the input tray. Print speed is fast enough for home and shop use. If you are looking for more paper capacity, super-fast printing, regular photo paper printing, well then invest in a more feature-packed costlier printer. For a home, student, shop purpose L130 is stupendous! I am yet to try on a photo paper, but that is “extra” start if I get a decent print. If not, I’m happy the way it is.Single-function is what you need today–Everyone has a decent smartphone that can scan and PDF documents using the camera. Free apps like Adobe Scan, Google Scan, CamScan, etc. can scan documents, align them, auto-correct colors, and will save you an extra 3-4K by buying a single-function (print only) printer. I see many reviews saying L130 is bad because it doesn’t scan! As it says, its a single function printer; it cannot scan.It’s an ink tank–If you do not want to fall prey for the ink cartridge scam, you need to go for an ink tan printer. Yes, ink tanks (like the L130) are a little expensive than inkjets cartridge printers, but in the long run, ink tank gets you the best return on investment (ROI). Inkjets are available for 2k and does max of 50-60 color prints. Making you buy another cartridge for 1.5k every 60 color prints. L130 can yield you 5000+ color (and 4000+ monochrome) prints in just one refill. The printer comes with 4 sets of colors, and technically you do not have to worry for a few months/years without an ink change.Compact for the desk–In its compact state (when trays are inside), the depth as less than 30 cms., making it ideal for any normal shelf/cabinet. Input trays also fits a 1 ft tall shelf. As needed, retract the trays to place the papers. See photos as it is easier to understand that way ;). By far, this is the most compact ink tank printer I’ve seen.Loves Apple as much as Windows–This printer works smoothly (including installation in under 3 minutes) in Windows 10 and macOS 10.14 (yes, Mojave too!). Many reviews and Q&As indicating L130 doesn’t support a Mac. Well, sorry wrong informers… it does support a Mac and all you need is to go to Epson’s website to get the right driver.Make it wireless if you have the right router–L130 is a non-Wi-Fi/non-wireless USB printer. A few years back, when I upgraded my W-Fi router to a dual band AC model, I went for a router with a USB port and with an inbuilt print server, though I never used that functionality till date. That decision came to use now! Yes, if you have a router with print server (and USB port), you can connect L130 to the router and use it wireless! One additional step beyond Epson’s driver setup is that you will need to install the router’s print utility/driver. Simple application you have to download from the router’s website and you have a USB printer that you can print directly from a PC/Mac connected to the WLAN.Take it to the cloud–Okay, now that you have realized that this is a print-only, home use, Mac friendly, and wireless “capable” printer, do you want to take it to the cloud? Meaning do you want to print from anywhere in the world? Well, folks, it is possible with some extra steps. As mentioned in my above bullet, if you have a router that has a print server and a USB port, make it connect to your WLAN. Once connected, register the printer to your Google Chrome account. Once registered, share the printer with any other Gmail accounts so that they too can print. For example, in my case, I registered my L130 in my Google account account using Chrome, and shared it with my family members’ Gmail ID. Now all of them can print from their Android, iOS, Amazon Fire, PC, Mac, from anywhere on the planet---as long as their devices and the printer at home is connected to the Internet.Well, that me after the third day of use, but 2 months or research. Good luck Amazonians!----------------2024 update, Since I misused the gadget I had to get another one. No fault of Epson. Interestingly, I bought the very same model again after 6 years. No other printer does a better job. And nope, I am not paid or sponsored ;)

review_text: An ink tank printer, also known as a continuous ink system (CIS) printer, is a type of inkjet printer that uses large ink tanks or reservoirs instead of traditional ink cartridges. Here are some of its uses and benefits:Uses:High-Volume Printing: Ink tank printers are suitable for high-volume printing needs, making them ideal for businesses, home offices, or individuals who print a lot of documents and images.Color Printing: They are capable of producing high-quality color prints, making them popular for photo printing, graphic design, and other applications that require vibrant colors.Versatility: Ink tank printers can handle a wide range of print media, including regular paper, photo paper, envelopes, and more.Wireless Connectivity: Many modern ink tank printers come with wireless connectivity options, such as Wi-Fi, enabling easy printing from various devices like smartphones and tablets.Economical: They are generally more cost-effective in the long run compared to traditional cartridge-based printers because the ink tanks can be refilled with bulk ink bottles, reducing the cost per page.Benefits:Lower Printing Costs: Ink tank printers offer a lower cost per page compared to inkjet printers with cartridges since you can buy ink in bulk bottles, which are often more affordable.Reduced Waste: With ink tank printers, there is less plastic waste generated because you don't need to replace cartridges frequently.Longer Print Runs: The larger ink tanks allow for longer print runs without the need for constant ink replacement.Consistent Print Quality: These printers often provide consistent print quality since the ink supply is more stable and less likely to run out mid-print.Easy Ink Monitoring: Many ink tank printers have transparent ink tanks, so you can easily see how much ink is left, ensuring you're never caught off guard by an empty cartridge.Customizable Ink Configuration: Some ink tank printers allow you to adjust the ink configuration to suit your printing needs, such as using extra ink for photos or text documents.In summary, ink tank printers are a cost-effective and efficient choice for those who require high-volume color printing and want to reduce printing costs and waste. They offer several benefits over traditional inkjet printers with cartridges, making them a popular choice for many users.

review_text: I bought this laptop expecting "budget business machine." What I got was a beige brick that somehow makes Comic Sans feel fast by comparison.Performance: Opening a browser tab feels like negotiating a hostage situation. I've seen glaciers move with more urgency than this thing boots up.Build Quality: The plastic chassis creaks if you look at it wrong. Within three months, the hinge started sounding like a rusty gate in a horror movie. Very atmospheric, not what I paid for.Battery Life: Advertised "all-day battery." review_title: Dell 15 Laptop - Excellent Specification, Volatile Pricing, and a 0% Battery Out of the Box
review_text: I placed the order for the 512 GB SSD variant of this Dell laptop on June 2, 2026. At the time of purchase, it was priced at ₹62,990. However, today it is selling for ₹56,990, a drop of ₹6,000 in just one day. Interestingly, on June 1, 2026, the same laptop was priced at ₹67,990. The pricing appears to be highly volatile, which is quite surprising.When I checked the manufacturing details on the Dell website, it showed a manufacturing date of February 22, 2026, which means the laptop was approximately 4.5 months old at the time of delivery. While this is not uncommon for electronic products, it is something prospective buyers may want to be aware of.Another concern was the battery condition upon arrival. When I tried to power on the laptop for the first time, the battery was at 0%, and the laptop would not turn on. I had to charge it for about 30 minutes before I could start using it. In my experience, I have never received a brand-new laptop with a completely discharged battery. It would have been preferable if the seller had ensured the battery had at least a minimal charge before shipping.As a precaution, I recorded the entire process—from unboxing to the first successful power-on. I will contact the seller regarding this issue and will update this review once I receive their response.The configuration of the laptop I received is as follows:Model: Dell 15 Laptop (DC15250)Processor: 13th Gen Intel Core i5-1334U (10 cores, up to 4.60 GHz, 64-bit)Memory: 16 GB DDR4 (1 × 16 GB, 2666 MT/s)Storage: 512 GB M.2 PCIe NVMe SSDDisplay: 15.6-inch FHD (1920 × 1080), 120 Hz, 250 nits, WVA Anti-Glare LED Backlit Narrow BorderGraphics: Intel UHD GraphicsKeyboard: Backlit KeyboardOperating System: Windows 11 Home Single Language (Lifetime)Office: Microsoft Office Home 2024 (Lifetime)Microsoft 365: 1-year subscriptionAntivirus: McAfee (12 months)Wireless: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) 2×2 MU-MIMOPower Adapter: 65 W AC Adapter (4.5 mm, E4)Battery: 3-cell, 41 WhPalm Rest: Platinum Silver (without fingerprint reader)Warranty: 1 Year onsite warranty from Dell (OEM)For those who are tech-savvy, please note that this laptop comes with a non-vPro processor, and the palm rest does not include a fingerprint reader.The laptop did not come with a carrying case or a mouse. It would have been better if the seller had bundled a carrying case and a mouse with the package.The Amazon packaging was good. The laptop arrived in two boxes (one box placed inside the other), providing adequate protection during transit. However, I was under the impression that I had opted for Open Box Delivery with OTP verification. The delivery person informed me that it was not an Open Box Delivery and asked me to share the OTP before handing over the laptop. I had little choice but to share the OTP, especially since he is the regular Amazon delivery associate in my area.I purchased this laptop under the buyback/exchange option by trading in my 10-year-old laptop, which was still in good working condition. Amazon offered ₹2,800 for the old laptop (though the exchange price was very less). The exchange process was smooth, and I had a very positive experience with the Amazon delivery person.I will update this review after using the laptop for a few months and share my experience regarding its performance, battery life, and overall reliability.

review_text: I have been using the Realme Buds T310 for about 3 months, and here is my honest review.Design & Comfort:The earbuds are lightweight, compact, and easy to carry around. The build quality feels solid for the price. The in-ear fit is comfortable, and I can wear them for long periods without any pain or discomfort.Sound Quality:The sound quality is decent for listening to music and watching movies. However, the Spatial Audio feature did not impress me much, as it doesn't create the immersive experience I expected.ANC Performance:The Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) performs well. It effectively reduces background noise and provides a good noise-cancellation experience for everyday use.Gaming Performance:This is where I was most disappointed. Despite the company claiming 45ms low latency, I experienced noticeable audio lag while playing games such as PUBG. The delay affects gameplay and makes the earbuds unsuitable for serious gaming.Battery Life:The battery life is another weak point. The company advertises up to 40 hours of battery backup, but in my usage, I only get around 1¼ days before needing to recharge. The actual battery performance falls short of expectations.Overall Verdict:The Realme Buds T310 is a comfortable pair of earbuds with decent sound quality and effective ANC. However, its gaming performance and battery life are disappointing compared to the company's claims. I would recommend it mainly for casual music listening and media consumption, but not for gaming enthusiasts.

category: Electronics > Headphones, Earbuds & Accessories > Headphones > Over-Ear
review_text: Writing review after 3 weeks of use.I do not own any other headphones, so can't compare to othersI primarily use it wired with laptop for work, also used wireless on Android phone and iPad wireless for tvshows, music and games.Its a long review but may tell you everything you need to knowFit and comfort : Headband has a thinner foam cover, did not cause discomfort but could have benefitted from a thicker or wider foam. Earcups have very nice foam. Soft and comfortable. However, will feel stuck to head after an hour and needs to be pulled to release the feel. Not too warm or sweaty. Can be worn with glasses , but they will get pinned to the head adjust for comfort after wearing the headphones. Clamping force is not bad, feels tight without squeezing head and feeling uncomfortable. It folds onto quite a small shape and can be easily put into a backpack with laptops, chargers and other daily stuff. A headphone case would have been nice, but there is none so we have to buy our own if its requiredBuild quality: Plastic earcups and headband with metal insert for size adjustment sliders and the pivot hooks also feel like metal. They feel reliable in the short time I have used them. Don't feel the good kind of tightness but don't move around on their own.Connectivity : usbc for analog audio works well on laptop. Able to connect multiple devices phone and tablet on Bluetooth. The audio needs to be paused and played when switching devices, doesnt do it automatically. Usb A to C charging cable is long but doesn't support audio so can only use for charging.Controls : the buttons work well. Manual needs to be downloaded from Noise website, will tell you how it works. Instructions are not on the box. Volume up down, power and pairing, ambient, noise canceling and normal mode, adjustable noise cancelling, music and game mode can all be done on the headphones, all buttons are on the right earcup.Sound quality : Voice focused, good for calls on office meeting apps, phone. Sounds good with voice focused content like TV shows and movies, music is fine, doesnt sound harsh. Bass is personal opinion, it sounds slightly hollow and boomy to me but may sound fine to others.Games would not revommend, the hollow sound makes it difficult to understand what's happening in games like bgmi, codm, etc. Game mode makes no noticeable difference. Bluetooth or wired mode makes no noticeable difference in game sounds.Noise cancelling and ambient mode : Noise cancelling is good for blocking low frequency sounds. It blocks sounds of air conditioning and traffic quite well. Not so great with high frequencies like voices. Male voices will get reduced noticeably, female voices seem to come through more. Horns in traffic will come through and can be heard. Ambient mode seems to let in all sounds, so voices will be present but can be a little mixed up with other things when other sounds are present.Other points: there is no app, which can be a plus or minus. There is no option to change controls or equalise sound, which apps help with. But apps can also make a mess of existing positives through a bad update. App support would have been good to have but at least no option for the brand to make it worse with a bad update.Overall opinions : its worthwhile for the price. There are wireless headphones for lesser that will probably have lesser features or quality. And better features and quality will come at a high price. Based on my experience with earphones, I don't think the headphones in the 5000 - 10000 RS range will offer much better and the real good stuff may come at 20000 RS and above

review_title: Great potential ruined by terrible product support and fit issues
review_text: I am updating my initial 5-star review down to 3 stars after using the Noise Airwave Max 5 for a full year. While these headphones started off strong, several major setbacks have cropped up over 12 months of daily use that make it hard to fully recommend them.​The Dealbreaker: Zero Replacement Cushions​The absolute biggest issue with these headphones is sustainability. After a year, the ear cushions naturally started to wear out. When I tried to find replacements, I discovered that Noise does not sell replacement cushions, and they are completely unavailable in the aftermarket. To make matters worse, I tried calling their customer service center multiple times to find a solution, and nobody picks up the phone. It is incredibly frustrating that a perfectly functional pair of headphones basically has to be thrown away just because the ear pads wore out.​Design & Fit: Not Gym-Friendly​If you are planning to use these for an active lifestyle, look elsewhere. The fit is very loose. It constantly slides off or completely falls off my head while running or working out at the gym. It simply lacks the clamping force needed to stay secure during any physical activity.​Performance Degradation​Sound Quality: Over time, the audio experience has settled into being just "average." It gets the job done for casual listening, but it won't impress anyone looking for deep clarity or punchy bass.​Gaming Mode: The low-latency gaming mode worked great out of the box, but after a year, the latency has noticeably slowed down compared to the initial days.​App Support: There is no companion app for this device, meaning you can't tweak the EQ, update the firmware, or customize the controls to try and improve the experience.​The Verdict​The Noise Airwave Max 5 is okay for sitting at a desk and casual use, but the lack of customer support, the loose fit during workouts, and the fact that you have to bin the entire headset once the ear cushions degrade makes it a disappointing long-term investment.

review_title: Title: 70% of BOSE QC45 at 20% of the cost
review_text: After using the Noise Airwave Max 5 for several days, I can confidently say this is one of the best value propositions in the ANC headphone market. At roughly 1/5th the price of the Bose QC45, you're getting a surprisingly capable set of cans that punch well above their weight class. (Incidentally, BOSE invested in NOISE, which prompted me to purchase this headset)Sound Quality: This is where the Airwave Max 5 truly shines. The sound quality matches the QC45 in almost every way that matters. Instrument separation is excellent, allowing you to pick out individual elements in complex tracks. The neutral sound signature is perfect for extended listening sessions without fatigue. Whether I'm listening to classical, rock, or electronic music, these headphones deliver a balanced, clear presentation that rivals headphones costing 5x more.Comfort: Here's where you feel the price difference. While the QC45 disappears on your head for 5+ hour sessions, the Airwave Max 5 starts feeling noticeable after about 90 minutes. The ear cushions lack the plush, cloud-like feeling of Bose's premium padding, creating more pressure points around the ears. For shorter listening sessions, this isn't a deal-breaker, but marathon listeners should take note.Battery Life: The claimed 80-hour battery life is impressive, and while I haven't fully depleted it to verify, I can confirm it significantly outlasts my QC45. I've gone days without charging during regular use, which is a huge convenience.Build Quality & Reliability: The Airwave Max 5 feels solidly built, but this is where the unknown factor comes in. My 2012 QC25 still works perfectly, and Bose's spare parts availability means I can keep them running indefinitely. Will the Airwave Max 5 last a decade? Will replacement ear pads be available in 5 years? Time will tell, but for budget-conscious buyers, this long-term uncertainty is worth considering.Microphone: The mic performs at about 70% of the QC45's capability - perfectly usable for calls and meetings. It's notably better than Sony's older XM3 (though Sony has since improved), handling background noise reasonably well.Verdict: At this price point, the Noise Airwave Max 5 is an easy recommendation for anyone wanting premium sound without the premium price tag. You're getting 70% of the Bose experience for 20% of the cost, which is an excellent value proposition. The main compromises are in comfort and unproven longevity, but if you can live with those limitations, these headphones offer remarkable bang for your buck.Perfect for: Budget-conscious audiophiles, students, or anyone wanting a capable second pair of ANC headphones.Skip if: You need all-day comfort or demand the peace of mind that comes with established brand reliability.

review_text: Yes, this bag shows quality, but I give 3.5 stars to this bag.The feel of the canvas is fantastic. Stitching is quite good all around. I think it'll last a long time before tearing off. Although not sure if the zip on the front pocket will stand the test of time, as it is a bit rough to use. It only means excess force will be applied to the zip and eventually it'll break sooner than later.I purchased this as I wanted a different look when compared to the fancy new age bags mostly being sold. This bag truly has a 'timeless' authentic feel to it. Whoever designed it has done a brilliant job with this one. The colour of the canvas is spot on. It a blend between khaki, dark brown with a hint of green. It just looks so much more elegant compared to the standard khaki or army green, black or whatever other. The size, the pockets, the magnetic buttons and the drawstring (including the drawstring closure - some reviewers complaint they didn't receive it. This one has it. See photo), all of it just fits so well for my requirement. The photos on the Amazon page just do not do the justice to how good the bag actually looks. A suggestion to F Gear here... please make sure photos are clicked under proper lighting, otherwise people could deter from purchasing this bag simply because they can't see the colours properly.Two key negatives. Firstly, the bag is not properly water resistant. The drops are visible so it seems water resistant but the moment you touch the drops, the water gets absorbed by the canvas. I don't believe this bag can stand rain. F-Gear, please consider making bags more resistant to the elements. With such fast lifestyles and all the electronic gadgets in the bag, nobody wants to have their belongings wet. Waterproofing is a basic requirement. Just for this I cut 1 star. The other half star is taken off for the print with different colour patches and slogans. Very kiddish for me.. good for university students though (I suppose). I think these prints alone takes away some of the elegance. All of a sudden, something loud is there shouting "look at me. look at me". I think if you just had that F-Gear logo in blue and brown border, that would highlight the bag in a nice way, but it's currently overdone. So overall 3.5 stars from my side. I'm going to probably use a heat gun or a paint remover to remove these print.

review_text: If you're on the lookout for a solid pair of wireless earphones, the OnePlus Bullets Z2 might just catch your eye. I've been using them for a while, and here's my honest take on what they have to offer.Connectivity & Ease of Use:Let’s start with one of the essentials—connectivity. The OnePlus Bullets Z2 nails it with seamless Bluetooth connectivity that just works. Pairing them with my phone was as simple as it gets, and once connected, they stay that way without any annoying drops. The button placement on the neckband is intuitive, and after a day or two of use, I could easily control playback without needing to glance down, thanks to muscle memory. It’s the kind of convenience you don’t realize you need until you have it.Sound Quality - Balanced Yet Personal:Now, onto the sound quality. As someone who values a balanced sound signature, I found the Z2 to be a great match for my taste. Whether I'm listening to some mellow jazz, electronic beats, or even rock, the sound remains well-rounded and crisp. The highs, mids, and lows don't overpower each other, making it perfect for those who don't want their ears blasted with bass or overwhelmed by treble.That said, sound quality is a subjective experience, and preferences can vary widely. If you're a bass head looking for those earth-shaking lows, you might find these a tad restrained. But if, like me, you appreciate a balanced output across genres, these will hit the right notes for you.Battery Life & Quick Charging - A Week of Peace:Battery life is another highlight. With moderate use—think about 1-2 hours daily—you can stretch a single charge to last an entire week. Even if you’re a heavy listener, using them for 6-8 hours straight, they can hold up for around 2-3 days before needing a recharge. And the quick charge feature is a lifesaver—just 10 minutes of charging gets you 2-4 hours of extra playtime, which is perfect for those “oops, I forgot to charge them” moments.Gaming & Low Latency - Smooth Experience:I spend a fair bit of time playing games like BGMI, and the low latency mode on the Bullets Z2 makes a noticeable difference. There's minimal lag between the visuals and the audio, which makes for a much more immersive gaming experience. It's not just about the sound being clear; it's also about it being on time, and these earphones deliver that pretty well.Comfort & Passive Noise Isolation:Comfort is key when it comes to neckbands, and the Z2 doesn’t disappoint. They come with multiple earbud sizes, so you can pick the one that fits snugly for you. While there’s no active noise cancellation (ANC) here, you can achieve a decent level of passive noise isolation by choosing the right ear tips. This makes a noticeable difference in cutting out background noise during commutes or at the office.App Experience & Annoying Blinking Light:Now, onto a couple of quirks. The Bullets Z2 uses the HeyMelody app, which offers additional features like custom sound settings. However, my unit just wouldn’t connect with the app, which was a bummer. So, any fancy tweaks you could make through the app were out of my reach, and I had to rely solely on the default Bluetooth pairing. While everything worked smoothly once connected, I feel like I missed out on some customization options that might have enhanced my experience.Another thing that bugged me was the small white light that blinks when the neckband is connected to a device. It might not seem like a big deal, but if you’re using the earphones in a dark room or while lying down, that blinking light can be pretty distracting. Plus, it probably drains the battery a bit, albeit a small amount. A simple option to turn this off in the app would’ve been a nice touch.Final Thoughts - A Solid Pick for Most, with Room for Improvement:Overall, the OnePlus Z2 delivers where it matters—good sound quality, reliable connectivity, and battery life that won’t have you constantly reaching for the charger. It’s not perfect, especially with the blinking light and app connectivity issues, but those are minor compared to the solid performance it offers. Plus, with the quick-charge feature and low-latency gaming experience, it’s hard not to appreciate the value you get.If you’re looking for a reliable neckband that blends style, comfort, and balanced audio, the OnePlus Bullets Z2 is definitely worth considering. It might not satisfy those who crave earth-shattering bass, but for most listeners, it's a worthy contender at its price point.
