category: Electronics > Headphones, Earbuds & Accessories > Headphones > In-Ear
review_text: The OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC is the latest addition to OnePlus' lineup of wireless earphones, offering significant upgrades over its predecessors. These in-ear Bluetooth earphones feature Hybrid Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) up to 45dB, bombastic bass driven by 12.4mm drivers, and a long-lasting battery life, all packed into an ergonomic design. With just 10 minutes of charging, you get up to 20 hours of music playback, making it an excellent choice for those who need a reliable and powerful audio device on the go. The product is available in the striking "Grand Green" color, adding a touch of style to its functional design.### Design and Build QualityThe design of the OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC reflects a balance between aesthetics and practicality. The "Grand Green" color gives it a unique, vibrant look that stands out without being overly flashy. The earphones are constructed from high-quality materials, ensuring durability while maintaining a lightweight profile.**Neckband Design:**The neckband design is both flexible and sturdy, making it comfortable for long-term wear. The earphones are designed to fit snugly in the ears, which is crucial for effective noise cancellation and bass response. The magnetic earbuds are a convenient feature, allowing the earphones to snap together when not in use, which prevents tangling and conserves battery by automatically pausing playback.**Ergonomics:**Ergonomics play a key role in the overall user experience of these earphones. The earbuds are designed to fit comfortably in the ear canal, providing a secure fit that helps to block out external noise even when the ANC is turned off. The lightweight neckband rests comfortably on the shoulders without causing discomfort, making these earphones suitable for extended use.**Build Quality:**The build quality of the Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC is commendable. The materials used feel premium, and the buttons on the neckband are tactile and responsive. The device is also IP55-rated, meaning it is resistant to dust and water splashes, making it suitable for workouts and outdoor use.### Sound QualityOne of the standout features of the OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC is its sound quality, particularly the bass. The 12.4mm dynamic drivers are larger than what is typically found in wireless earphones, and this translates to a rich, deep bass response that is ideal for bass-heavy genres like EDM, hip-hop, and pop.**Bass Response:**The bass on these earphones is described as "bombastic," and rightly so. The 12.4mm drivers deliver a powerful low-end that doesn’t overshadow the mids and highs but rather complements them. The bass is punchy and clear, providing a satisfying thump that many users will appreciate, especially during workouts or while commuting.**Mid and High Frequencies:**The midrange is well-represented, with vocals and instruments coming through clearly without being drowned out by the bass. The highs are crisp and detailed, offering a balanced sound signature that is versatile enough for various music genres. However, some audiophiles might find the emphasis on bass slightly overpowering for more acoustic or classical tracks.**Active Noise Cancellation:**The Hybrid ANC technology in the Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC is capable of reducing ambient noise by up to 45dB. This feature works exceptionally well in environments with consistent background noise, such as on public transport or in a busy office. The ANC feature not only enhances the listening experience by minimizing distractions but also allows for lower volume levels, which can help in reducing ear fatigue over time.### Battery LifeBattery life is another area where the OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC excels. The earphones offer up to 28 hours of total battery life on a full charge, which is more than sufficient for daily use. This endurance makes them ideal for long commutes, travel, or extended use throughout the day.**Fast Charging:**One of the most impressive aspects of these earphones is their fast charging capability. With just 10 minutes of charging, you can get up to 20 hours of playback time. This feature is particularly useful for those who are often on the move and need a quick top-up before heading out. The full charge time is also relatively short, allowing the earphones to be fully charged in less than an hour.**Usage with ANC:**When using ANC, the battery life is understandably reduced, but it still remains impressive. With ANC turned on, you can expect around 18 to 20 hours of playback, which is still above average compared to other wireless earphones in the market. The battery life makes these earphones highly reliable, reducing the need for frequent recharges.### Connectivity and ControlsThe OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC offers seamless connectivity with Bluetooth 5.0, ensuring a stable connection with minimal latency. The earphones are easy to pair with both Android and iOS devices, although they work particularly well with OnePlus smartphones, which can unlock additional features like quick pairing and battery status notifications.**Latency:**For those who enjoy gaming or watching videos on their mobile devices, low latency is a crucial factor. The Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC performs well in this regard, with minimal lag that ensures audio syncs well with video content. This makes them suitable not just for music but also for multimedia consumption.**Controls:**The inline controls on the neckband are intuitive and easy to use. The buttons allow for controlling playback, adjusting volume, taking calls, and activating voice assistants. The buttons are well-placed and provide good feedback, making it easy to use the controls without needing to look at them. The earphones also support quick switching between two paired devices, a handy feature for those who frequently switch between their phone and laptop.**Call Quality:**The Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC features a built-in microphone that provides clear voice transmission during calls. The noise cancellation technology also extends to call quality, effectively reducing background noise so that your voice comes through clearly even in noisy environments. This makes the earphones suitable for professional use, such as conference calls or virtual meetings.### Additional FeaturesThe OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC comes with several additional features that enhance the overall user experience:**Environmental Noise Cancellation (ENC):**While ANC helps block out external noise during music playback, the Environmental Noise Cancellation (ENC) technology focuses on improving call quality by reducing background noise during calls. This ensures that your voice is heard clearly on the other end, even in noisy environments.**Magnetic Control:**The magnetic control feature automatically pauses music playback when the earbuds are snapped together and resumes when they are separated. This not only helps conserve battery life but also adds convenience, especially when you need to quickly pause and resume your music.**Voice Assistant Support:**The earphones support voice assistants like Google Assistant and Siri, allowing for hands-free control of your device. This is particularly useful when you need to make a call, send a message, or get directions without reaching for your phone.### Comfort and FitComfort is a crucial aspect of any in-ear earphones, and the Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC scores well in this department. The earphones come with multiple sizes of silicone ear tips, ensuring a secure and comfortable fit for different ear shapes. The snug fit also helps with passive noise isolation, further enhancing the effectiveness of the ANC feature.**Weight and Wearability:**The earphones are lightweight, making them comfortable to wear for extended periods without causing ear fatigue. The neckband design distributes the weight evenly across the shoulders, preventing the earphones from feeling heavy or cumbersome.**Suitability for Sports and Workouts:**Thanks to the IP55 rating, the Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC is resistant to sweat and water, making them suitable for workouts and outdoor activities. The secure fit ensures that the earphones stay in place during physical activity, providing a reliable audio experience even during intense exercise.### Price and Value for MoneyThe OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC is priced competitively, offering excellent value for money given its feature set. It is positioned in the mid-range segment, making it accessible to a wide range of users while still providing premium features such as Hybrid ANC, powerful bass, and long battery life.**Comparison with Competitors:**When compared to other wireless earphones in the same price range, the Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC holds its own, if not outperforms, many competitors. The combination of sound quality, build, and features like fast charging and ANC make it a strong contender in the market. Competitors like the Realme Buds Wireless and JBL Tune series offer similar features, but the overall package of the Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC is more refined, especially in terms of bass performance and battery life.**Long-Term Value:**Considering the durability, battery life, and sound quality, the Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC represents a long-term investment. review_text: There is nothing wrong with the looks of the Bullets Z2, they are actually quite decent looking. They are just a neckband, and this is what neckbands look like, and we have made our peace with it. The middle part is a thicker, slightly more stiff, U shaped-silicon band, with two chunky pill-shaped units at the end. The wires stem from these pills and have earbuds on the end. One of these pill-shaped units houses the battery, while the other has control options and the USB Type C port on the side. You get volume buttons on this control unit and a multi-function play/pause button. The battery unit has the OnePlus branding and the logo, while the volume buttons are highlighted in red.The earbuds on the end are pretty standard, with eartips on one side and a flat back with magnets. When the buds are attached together, they will simply stop playing the audio, which you can resume once you put them back in. The Bullets Wireless Z2 are quite light and can be worn around the neck all day without ever feeling like a burden. The material used is quite skin-friendly and feels quite sturdy as well. It also comes with an IP55 rating.Pairing the OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 is a pretty fuss-free process. All you have to do is press and hold the play/pause button, and the buds will go into pairing mode. You can then look up the buds in the list of Bluetooth pairings on your device and connect the buds. Once connected, the Bullets Z2 will connect to your phone automatically once you put them on.You get the usual volume buttons on the buds and another button in the middle in terms of controls. Now instead of simply sharing the command load amongst its button comrades, OnePlus has put all the burden on this one button in the middle. Apart from the usual pairing/play/ pause/ call receiving/ call ending functions (which are already a lot for a single button), OnePlus has also made it responsible for changing tracks. You have to press the button twice to skip to the next song and thrice to go back to the last song. It may all sound simple but can actually be chaotic in practice as you have to keep track of how many times you have pressed that tiny button before the command is completed.The OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 comes with the biggest drivers seen on a pair of OnePlus earphones- 12.4mm. The fact that OnePlus is offering such big drivers for under two thousand rupees is a major plus point for the buds. The earbuds support two audio codecs, SBC and AAC.As for the audio performance, the Bullets Wireless Z2 are pretty loud and come with plenty of bass, something that seems to be every brand’s audio formula in the budget segment. While this kind of signature sound gives the audio some faux body, it actually fails to deliver what the audio is truly supposed to sound like.If you are someone looking for a pair of earphones that offer balanced sound, then you might not like the sound profile that the Bullets Wireless Z2 offer as they lack balance, majorly.That said, if you are someone who likes bass-heavy audio output and do not mind if some bass sneaks into your mids, then the OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 will definitely be your cup of tea.The OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 were pretty good in terms of call quality. We could hear the speaker clearly, and we heard no complaints whatsoever regarding our audio quality while using the buds. As the buds fit deep into your ear canals, they offer really good passive noise cancellation.They come with big 12.4 mm drivers, offer really long battery life, have a bass-heavy signature sound, and have a really solid build. But because the earbuds are really bass-heavy, they lack balance, and for those who like to listen to melodious or classical music, these might not be a great option.The Bullets Wireless Z2 also face some heat from the likes of Oppo Enco M32 and the Realme Buds 2, which are priced in the same vicinity. The OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 are actually a great proposition for the price; you only need to have a liking for bass.

review_text: I was initially very impressed with the OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2. The sound quality was decent for the price, the battery life was excellent, and they were comfortable to wear. I liked my first pair so much that I ended up purchasing a second one for another family member.However, my experience took a sharp downturn after a few months of normal usage. On my first headset, the audio in one earbud started cutting out and became distorted. Within a week, it went completely silent. A few days later, the second earbud followed the exact same pattern, rendering the entire headset useless.Thinking it might have been a one-off defect, I wasn't too concerned. But to my dismay, the second headset I purchased developed the exact same issue after a similar period of use. First one side failed, then the other.The problem seems to be a clear and consistent design flaw at the point where the thin earphone wire joins the thicker part of the neckband. As you can see in the photo I've attached, this joint is a weak point. If I wiggle the wire at that specific spot, the sound momentarily comes back, which confirms it's a fragile internal connection that breaks with regular, everyday use.For this critical failure to happen on two separate units in the exact same way is unacceptable. While the features are good on paper, the product is completely let down by poor durability and a short lifespan.Verdict: I cannot recommend the OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2. It's a shame because they are great while they work, but they seem designed to fail. Save your money and invest in something more reliable.

review_text: I had used a OnePlus neckband about four years ago, and I was very satisfied with its quality. That positive experience was the main reason I decided to purchase a OnePlus product again.However, I am extremely disappointed with the OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 ANC. The call quality is not clear at all. Whenever I attend a call, the person on the other side is unable to hear me clearly, which makes the product very difficult to use for calls.Since this was an open-box product, I understand that a return may not be possible. However, there is also no option available to replace the product. This is particularly disappointing because the issue may be specific to the unit I received.With open-box products, customers usually check for physical damage, basic functionality, and sound quality at the time of delivery. But issues such as poor microphone/call quality can only be properly identified after using the product for a day or two.Therefore, I am completely unsatisfied with the product I received.

review_title: Extremely disappointed with the call quality of the newer version
review_text: I have been using OnePlus neckband earphones for years. My previous OnePlus Z2 ANC worked really well for almost two years. The sound quality was good, the overall experience was reliable, and I was genuinely happy with it. The only issue that developed later was that the person on the other end of a call could no longer hear me properly.Because of that, I decided to upgrade to the newer version with AI Noise Cancellation, expecting the call quality to be even better.Unfortunately, it has been the complete opposite.The call quality is extremely disappointing, especially while riding a bike. The person on the other end could barely hear me, and at times could not hear me at all. Despite the advertised AI noise cancellation, the microphone performance in real-world outdoor conditions is nowhere close to what I expected.What makes this more frustrating is that the Amazon rating/reviews are combined for different OnePlus neckband variants, so the overall rating looks excellent but does not necessarily represent the performance of this particular model. I bought this expecting an upgrade from my previous OnePlus neckband, but for calls, it feels like a downgrade.If your primary requirement is good call quality while travelling or riding outdoors, I would strongly recommend thinking twice before buying this one.The older OnePlus neckband was genuinely good. Unfortunately, I cannot say the same about this newer version.

review_text: The product is very good as mentioned in all other reviews, but they have purposely made the joint connecting the wire with earbuds out of cheap quality rubber. Plus, there is no clear warranty document that mentions or defines what damage is. Instead of listening to the complain, the service centre people question you and then say how do we know how you are using it. They just deny and twist words without having any explanation of what they mean in particular. Basically, the service centre policy is 'its our policy to call a cat a dog.' According to them, even hard evidence will not get them to admit something because it's their policy to dodge question. I asked them why the other side is coming off like powder and little chips of rubber, like paint, they say it's because of how you use it. Then I say do you see any scratches on the earphone? review_text: I’ve been using Samsung smartphones for many years, and I’ve always been happy with the overall experience. review_text: Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra – Excellent Upgrade from S22 UltraI moved to the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra after using the S22 Ultra for almost 4 years. Unfortunately, my S22 Ultra suddenly stopped working one day, don't know the reason of the damage, so I had to replace it and decided to go with the S25 Ultra.After using the S25 Ultra, I can confidently say that the upgrade has been excellent.The first thing I noticed is the weight and feel of the phone. Although it has a large 6.9-inch display and a 5,000 mAh battery, it feels noticeably lighter and more comfortable than my S22 Ultra. Samsung lists the S25 Ultra at 218 g, compared with 229 g for the S22 Ultra.What I like most1. Customization – ExcellentThis is probably the thing I like most about Samsung phones. The level of customization available is incredible. You can customize the home screen, lock screen, widgets, themes, icons, gestures, Edge panels, Always-On Display and many other aspects.There is almost no limit to how much you can personalize the phone.This is one area where I feel Samsung is far ahead of many other smartphones.2. Display – ExcellentThe display is absolutely beautiful. It is crisp, bright and smooth, and the 120 Hz refresh rate makes everything feel very fluid. The 6.9-inch QHD+ Dynamic AMOLED 2X display is one of the biggest strengths of the phone.3. Sound – Very goodThe speaker quality is also very impressive. Music, YouTube, calls and videos sound clear and powerful for a smartphone.4. Performance – ExcellentComing from the S22 Ultra, the S25 Ultra feels significantly faster and smoother in everyday use. Apps open quickly, multitasking is excellent and the phone handles demanding applications without any noticeable slowdown.Samsung uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite for Galaxy, along with an improved cooling system, which helps with sustained performance.5. Camera – ExcellentThe camera system is another major improvement. The 200 MP main camera and the new 50 MP ultra-wide camera provide excellent detail and versatility. Samsung has also improved night photography and video processing.6. S PenS Pen – One Step Back from S22 UltraThe S Pen is still one of the unique advantages of the Ultra series, and I use it regularly for notes, screenshots, editing and precise interaction with the phone.However, this is one area where I feel the S25 Ultra is actually a downgrade compared with my S22 Ultra.My S22 Ultra S Pen had Bluetooth and Air Actions, which meant I could use the S Pen as a remote shutter button for the camera. I especially used this feature for group selfies and taking photos from a distance. It was genuinely useful and one of the features I loved about the S Pen.Unfortunately, the S25 Ultra S Pen no longer has Bluetooth, so the remote camera shutter and Air Actions are no longer available.For me, this is a significant miss. Samsung has improved the phone in many areas, but removing a useful feature that was already available on the S22 Ultra feels like a step backwards.I really hope Samsung brings Bluetooth and remote-camera functionality back to the S Pen in future Ultra models.One disappointment – Amazon sale pricingThe one thing I was not happy about was the Amazon sale pricing.I was monitoring the phone price before purchasing. Just one day before the sale, the price was around ₹89,899. On the actual sale day, the price increased to ₹94,999, and then the exchange offer was presented as an additional benefit.This made me question the actual value of the so-called sale.In my experience, the sale did not feel like a genuine special offer, because the price was actually lower before the sale started. Customers who track prices can easily notice this.I would therefore recommend that buyers check the price history for a few days before purchasing during an Amazon sale, rather than assuming that the displayed "sale price" is necessarily the best price.OverallComing from an S22 Ultra that I used for nearly four years, I am very happy with the S25 Ultra.

review_text: ​I’ve been daily driving the S25 Ultra for a solid three months now, and the honeymoon phase is officially over. review_title: Samsung S25 Ultra Front Camera Fogging Issue
review_text: Hi everyone,I bought S25 Ultra from Amazon on 6th July. Unfortunately, my return period has already ended. I didn't use the phone much during the first few days because I was waiting for my case and screen protector to arrive.When I finally started using the front camera, I noticed a very strange issue. After opening the selfie camera, everything looks normal at first. But within about 20 seconds, the front camera suddenly becomes foggy, and the image turns gray and blurry, making it almost unusable.As soon as I close the camera, the fogging disappears. If I wait for some time (around 5 minutes) and open the front camera again, the exact same thing happens.I have already tried resetting the camera settings, but the issue still comes back.This is really disappointing, especially for such an expensive flagship phone. Samsung community members are telling that it's manufacturing defect. Since my Amazon return window has already expired, I'm worried about what to do next.I contacted Samsung Customer care. Instead of offering a replacement, I was told to visit a Samsung Service Center to get the phone repaired.This is completely unacceptable. I bought a brand new flagship phone, and within just 13 days I'm being asked to repair it because of what appears to be a manufacturing defect. A premium device should not need repairs immediately after purchase.What is even more concerning is that I have read several posts on Reddit and the Samsung Community where users reported that even after the phone was repaired, the same issue returned. If that's true, then repairing the device is not a real solution.As a customer, I paid for a brand new phone, not a repaired one. I expect Samsung to provide a proper resolution, such as a replacement, instead of asking customers to accept repairs on a newly purchased device.This has been a very disappointing experience, and I hope Samsung takes responsibility and resolves this issue fairly.

review_text: This has been a disappointing purchase. I had previously used OnePlus Nord Buds 2r for more than two years and they were excellent. Naturally, I gravitated towards the 3r variant of the same line assuming that the past would dictate the future. Unfortunately enough, that was not true.The good:- It will connect to multiple devices at once so no hassle with the constant disconnecting and connecting.- It produces sound.The bad:- The set up process is frustrating. For phones, you need to have this HeyMelody app installed to even discover and connect the device. For laptops, I don't even know how the pairing works. If I ever need to unpair the buds from my laptop, it is a sisyphean task, a game where I try random methods until it somehow connects.- It will connect to multiple devices at once. You might notice that this point was in "the good" section too. Dear reader, yes, you are right. The one-to-many connection feature falls apart more often than not. If I am listening to some music playing on my phone and I get a notification on my laptop, my phone's audio is gone. I am not getting it back unless I forcefully disconnect and connect my phone.- Randomly, it will show that the buds are connected to the laptop but the laptop won't have the buds listed as an audio device. Now you need to scrounge for answers, trying throwing things at wall until they fix because I don't know why they are built this way.- The body is weak. The plastic body easily gets scratches from my finger nails. It's not even been a whole month and the body is squeaking when I press it.TLDR: Don't buy them. These buds are plagued by their own "features". I should have just brought the older generation.

review_title: Fantastic battery, stunning display, and solid daily performance
review_text: After 2 full weeks of daily use, here is my honest review of the OnePlus Nord CE6. It’s a rock-solid device in most scenarios, especially if you prioritize battery and media consumption.## The Pros:Battery Life (The Biggest Highlight): The battery is a beast. With mixed usage, it easily lasts me 2 full days. Even on heavy usage days, it clears a full day with zero issues, and the fast charging tops it up in no time.Display & Design: The screen is gorgeous with incredibly minimal bezels. It looks premium and catches people's attention—I've actually had people ask me what phone it is. The big screen is perfect for content consumption. I have the blue color, and the minimal design looks great.Durability: Build quality is top-notch. It has already survived 1–2 accidental drops without a single scratch or issue.Performance: Oxygen OS is highly refined and keeps everything feeling butter-smooth in daily tasks. Gaming performance is solid, and features like performance mode, voice changer, and especially bypass charging are incredibly useful.Sound Quality: Dual speakers sound awesome. The 300% volume mode is a lifesaver in noisy environments; I find myself using it every single day.Main Camera: Both the front and rear cameras click sharp, vibrant, social-media-ready photos right out of the box.## The Cons:No Ultra-Wide Lens: The only real downside for me is the lack of an ultra-wide camera. I definitely miss having that option for landscape shots.

review_title: Absolute Battery Monster & Blazing Fast Charging – The King of Practicality!
review_text: I recently switched to the OnePlus Nord CE6 after a brief stint with the Nothing Phone 3A Pro (and having unluckily lost my Nord CE4 before that). While the Nothing phone was aesthetically brilliant with great cameras, it heavily missed the mark on daily battery endurance and charging speed for my usage. Moving back to this OnePlus device has been an absolute game-changer.Here is my breakdown after putting the device through its paces (According to my experiences and usage patterns) :🔋 Battery Life: Elite Tier EnduranceThe battery performance on this phone is a literal joke—in the best way possible. On day one alone (while the phone was still indexing and setting up accounts), I hit an unbelievable 8 hours and 31 minutes of Screen-On Time (SOT), and I still had 26% battery remaining! The system estimated another 9 hours of standby on Balanced Mode. The overnight idle drain is practically flat. You can easily clear a 24-hour cycle and push past 10+ hours of heavy SOT before needing a plug.⚡ Charging: The Return of True Fast ChargingHaving to charge my previous 5000 mAh phone twice every 36 hours was becoming a chore. Getting back to the legendary high-speed SUPERVOOC charging ecosystem feels incredibly liberating. Top-ups are ridiculously quick, giving you absolute peace of mind without having to constantly hunt for a wall socket.📱 Software & Convenience FeaturesComing back to OxygenOS feels highly optimized. Little daily conveniences work perfectly here. For instance, taking a scrolling screenshot happens smoothly in a single action, unlike other custom UIs that clunkily force you to take multiple manual captures just to stitch an image together. The system launcher and background management are fluid and snappy out of the box.📦 Storage Efficiency (8GB/128GB Variant)While I am stepping down to 128 GB after using 256 GB phones for a few years, managing it is completely effortless if you manage your data dynamically. With streaming being so seamless and offloading data to a laptop being a breeze, 128 GB is more than enough for current essential usage and apps, especially if you aren’t heavily into hoarding photography.Final Verdict:If you value raw battery longevity, minimal idle drain, lightning-fast charging speeds, and a reliable, snappy daily user experience, the OnePlus Nord CE6 is an absolute home run. Highly recommended!Shall update after a month with a more specific review.

review_title: Excellent performance, display and battery life
review_text: The OnePlus Nord CE6 is an impressive phone with a strong combination of performance, battery life, display quality, and features. The Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 processor with 8GB RAM handles everyday apps, multitasking, gaming, and streaming smoothly.The 8000mAh battery is one of the biggest highlights. The phone can comfortably last through a long day, and the large battery is especially useful for users who don't want to charge frequently.The 1.5K 144Hz AMOLED display looks excellent, with sharp details, vibrant colours, deep blacks, and smooth scrolling. The high refresh rate also makes gaming and general navigation feel very responsive.The 50MP main camera and 32MP selfie camera deliver good results, particularly in daylight. The ability to record 4K video is a useful addition for users who regularly shoot photos and videos. Low-light performance can vary, but overall camera performance is good for the segment.The phone feels well-built and durable, and the extensive IP66/IP68/IP69/IP69K protection provides additional confidence against dust and water exposure. The Fresh Blue finish also gives it a premium and attractive appearance.With 256GB storage, there is plenty of space for apps, photos, videos, and games. review_title: Great Performance and Battery, But Heavy in the Hand
review_text: The OnePlus Nord CE 6 truly excels in its everyday operational capabilities, offering a consistently smooth and responsive user experience. From launching applications to multitasking between various demanding programs, its performance remains remarkably robust and reliable. This device handles daily digital tasks with effortless grace, providing a fluidity that users will undoubtedly appreciate. Beyond its commendable processing power, the battery life of the OnePlus Nord CE 6 stands out as a particular highlight. It is engineered to comfortably last throughout an entire day of typical usage, alleviating the common anxiety associated with frequently searching for charging points. Whether you're streaming content, browsing the web, engaging with social media, or making numerous calls, this smartphone provides sustained power without interruption, making it a dependable companion for even the busiest schedules.However, this impressive performance and longevity come with a notable trade-off in terms of physical design: the device is quite heavy. This substantial weight becomes particularly apparent during extended periods of single-handed use. Imagine holding the phone up to your ear for a lengthy conversation, or gripping it tightly while navigating a busy street and trying to read a message – the strain on your hand and wrist can quickly escalate. The sheer heft of the OnePlus Nord CE 6, while perhaps contributing to a perception of build quality, means that operating it comfortably with just one hand for prolonged durations can become an uncomfortable, even tiring, endeavor. This ergonomic consideration is important for users who spend a significant amount of time interacting with their devices, as the physical discomfort could detract from an otherwise excellent user experience.

review_title: Extremely disappointing – One of the worst OnePlus phones I have used in 10 years
review_text: I have been a OnePlus user for nearly 10 years, and OnePlus has always been one of the brands I trusted for a smooth, reliable and hassle-free smartphone experience. I have used and recommended OnePlus phones for years.Unfortunately, the OnePlus Nord CE6 5G (8GB RAM + 256GB, Fresh Blue) has been a completely different experience.This is honestly one of the most disappointing OnePlus phones I have ever purchased, and for the first time in nearly a decade, this phone has made me seriously reconsider buying a OnePlus device again.1. Heating issue during normal usageThe phone gets noticeably warm during regular usage. I am not talking about heavy gaming or extreme workloads.The heating happens during normal day-to-day activities, which is disappointing for a phone with a modern chipset and a large battery.A smartphone at this price should be able to handle basic tasks without becoming noticeably warm.2. Phone suddenly hangs while using itThe most frustrating issue is that the phone suddenly becomes unresponsive/hangs while I am using it.At times, the phone simply does not respond properly, and I have to wait for it to recover. This is extremely irritating when you are doing something important.With 8GB RAM and 256GB storage, I expected smooth multitasking and reliable performance. Instead, I am experiencing random freezes and interruptions during normal usage.3. Fingerprint authentication fails during paymentThis is one of my biggest concerns.While trying to make payments through payment gateways/apps, the fingerprint authentication does not work properly. The fingerprint lock/authentication sometimes fails when I actually need it.This is not a minor inconvenience. Today, smartphones are used for UPI payments, banking, online shopping and other financial transactions. If biometric authentication does not work reliably during a payment, it becomes a serious usability and trust issue.The fingerprint sensor may work in some normal unlocking situations, but my experience during payment authentication has been disappointing.4. Frequent app crashesAnother major problem is frequent application crashes and unexpected app behaviour.The issue is not limited to one particular application.For example, while using Google Maps, I have experienced situations where the application does not work as expected. Maps is one of the most basic and commonly used applications on a smartphone, so having problems while using it is extremely frustrating.I have also experienced apps becoming unresponsive or closing unexpectedly.5. Not the OnePlus experience I expectedWhat makes this even more disappointing is the fact that I am a long-time OnePlus customer.I bought this phone expecting the same smooth OxygenOS experience and reliability that I have associated with OnePlus for years.Instead, I am facing:- ❌ Heating during normal usage- ❌ Random hanging/freezing- ❌ Frequent app crashes- ❌ Google Maps not working as expected- ❌ Fingerprint authentication issues during payments- ❌ Overall unreliable day-to-day experienceThese are not features I am complaining about. These are basic smartphone functions that I expect to work properly.My message to OnePlusI genuinely hope OnePlus takes feedback like this seriously.I have been loyal to the brand for almost a decade, and I have recommended OnePlus phones to friends and family because of my previous experiences.But the Nord CE6 has changed my perception of the brand.I understand that every individual device can potentially have a manufacturing defect or software issue. However, as a customer, I should not have to deal with freezing, application crashes, heating and payment authentication problems on a new smartphone.I would strongly recommend OnePlus investigate these issues through software updates and, where necessary, provide proper service/support for affected customers.Final verdictI would not recommend the OnePlus Nord CE6 based on my personal experience.The specifications on paper may look impressive, but specifications are meaningless if the phone cannot provide a stable and reliable everyday experience.For a long-time OnePlus customer like me, this is particularly disappointing.I am giving 2 stars only because there are some good aspects of the phone, but the basic reliability issues I am experiencing significantly affect my overall experience.OnePlus, after almost 10 years of being your customer, this is the first phone that has made me question whether I should buy OnePlus again.

review_title: Unsafe Product: Loud Pop Burning Smell
review_text: DO NOT BUY!!!Very disappointed with Samsung's charger quality and after-sales support.I have purchased two original Samsung 45W chargers—one from a Samsung Store and another from the Samsung Store on Amazon. Unfortunately, both have failed.The Amazon charger lasted only 10 months. What is even more concerning is that my phone was not connected to it. The charger was simply plugged into the wall socket with the switch turned on when I heard a loud spark/pop, followed immediately by a strong burning smell from the charging brick. This is a serious safety concern.My previous Samsung charger also stopped working, making this the second original Samsung charger to fail.I am also disappointed with Samsung's warranty process. Even minor cosmetic dents or marks can be treated as "physical damage," which may result in warranty claims being denied, even when the issue is clearly an internal electrical failure. Chargers are portable accessories, so minor signs of normal use should not automatically disqualify customers from warranty support.Finally, I have concerns about the charger I bought from the Samsung Store on Amazon. I cannot say whether it was genuine or not, but the packaging looked old and appeared to have been tampered with, with stickers seemingly reapplied over other labels. I needed the charger urgently, so I kept it at the time. Looking back after this incident, I believe Samsung and Amazon should investigate such cases more carefully to ensure customers receive brand-new, untampered products.After two charger failures—including one that sparked and emitted a burning smell—I have lost confidence in Samsung's charger quality and hope both Samsung and Amazon improve their quality control and customer support.

I've already had to add some tape for better grip.I'm concerned that repeatedly pulling the cable like this could eventually damage the earphones.Overall, good sound and excellent comfort, but the Type-C connector design needs better grip. review_title: Excellent Colors & Overall Experience Under ₹40K, But Know the Trade-offs
review_text: I spent nearly a month comparing TVs, visiting stores multiple times, watching reviews, and reading long-term owner experiences before making this purchase. Every opinion below is based entirely on my own real-world experience.Pros:Excellent color reproduction. To my eyes: LG 90/100, Samsung 95/100, Sony 100/100. Sony still has the best picture processing, but Samsung comes surprisingly close for much less money.Smooth and responsive Tizen OS.Excellent Bluetooth headphone audio quality.HDR content looks vibrant and natural.Very good browser performance.HDMI ARC/eARC works perfectly.Cons:Motion isn't quite as smooth as LG's implementation. I noticed some ghosting/trailing, especially with subtitles and certain animated content.Black bars are more noticeable in a dark room because this is a Direct LED TV.No native Kodi or Jellyfin app on Tizen (Plex is available).Built-in USB media player doesn't support every subtitle format.Smart Hub shows recommendations and promotional content that can't be completely removed.I also spent time comparing TCL and Xiaomi TVs. Their Mini LED models definitely offer better black levels and HDR, but I personally found their color tuning too aggressive and oversaturated. They look impressive in a showroom, but for long viewing sessions I preferred Samsung's more natural image. Sony still delivers the best picture overall, but it also costs significantly more.Final Verdict: If you can get this TV for around ₹40,000–45,000 (or even less with bank offers and coupons), I think it's an excellent value. I personally wouldn't recommend paying much more than that, because above this price range there are stronger alternatives. If your priorities are natural colors, a smooth interface and reliable day-to-day performance, this TV is easy to recommend. If you need Mini LED blacks, Kodi/Jellyfin support or advanced USB media playback, you should consider an Android TV platform or an external streaming device.

review_title: Honest Review After Researching Multiple Brands
review_text: After doing a lot of research and comparing TVs in the under ₹40,000 segment, I shortlisted brands like Samsung, TCL, Xiaomi (Mi), and Vu. Honestly, brands like TCL, Xiaomi, and Vu offer better specifications, excellent displays, and great value for money at this price point. However, I wasn't completely confident about their long-term reliability and after sales service. That's why I finally chose Samsung, a brand that has built trust over the years.I purchased this TV for around ₹36,000 during an offer, which I feel is a decent deal for a Samsung Mini-LED TV.Installation ExperienceOne thing buyers should know is that the box does not include a table stand or wall mount separately packed. During installation, Samsung provides the option to choose either a table-top installation or wall mounting.Unfortunately, my installation experience wasn't perfect. The Samsung service engineer informed my family that the TV stand was not provided by the company and charged ₹2,700 for a wall mount setup. Since I was not at home during the installation, I asked him to complete the work and paid the amount later. Afterward, I learned that the installation option I chose should have been provided without the extra charge. I immediately raised a complaint with both Amazon and Samsung Customer Care.To Samsung's credit, their customer service was excellent. They acted quickly, instructed the service engineer to refund the amount, and the refund was processed promptly. I really appreciate Samsung for taking strict action and resolving the issue professionally.TV Performance•Build Quality: Good and feels premium.•Picture Quality: Decent, but not exceptional. I expected a bit more from the Mini-LED panel.•Sound Quality: Surprisingly impressive. The 30W speakers are excellent, and for most users, there is no need to invest in a separate soundbar.My viewOverall, this is a good and reliable TV from a trusted brand. If brand reputation, service support, and peace of mind are important to you, Samsung is a solid choice.However, if you're not particularly attached to a brand name and want maximum features and picture quality for your money, I would also recommend considering TCL, Xiaomi (Mi), and Vu, as they offer excellent value in this price range.And finally, when it comes to TVs, my heart still says Sony is the king. If your budget allows, Sony remains my first preference any day..

review_text: I purchased the boAt Rockerz 250 Pro+ and, considering the price, it offers good value for money. The build quality also feels good and durable.However, there are a few drawbacks. The magnetic earbuds do not automatically power off or disconnect when attached together. Instead, I have to manually long-press the button to disconnect and switch off the neckband. Similarly, when separating the magnetic earbuds, they do not automatically reconnect; I need to long-press the button again to connect the device.Another disappointment is the lack of Transparency Mode and Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) options. The product specifications and app experience can be confusing, but I could not find any option to enable Transparency Mode or ANC in the boAt app for the Rockerz 250 Pro+.Overall, the neckband delivers good sound quality and build quality for its price, but the missing auto magnetic connect/disconnect feature and the absence of Transparency Mode and ANC reduce the overall convenience.

review_text: The media could not be loaded. Used this watch for over a month now.. Bought it during the first sale.. Keep reading for an unbiased review and tips/tricks to ensure all the functions in the watch are working smoothly.1) Large Curved Display in this price category - 1.69 inch2) Battery with heavy usage and frequently waking up the screen, alexa, alarms, notifications is about 3 days. On standby while just checking the time occassionally is about 8 days. Pretty good. Full charging time is about 1.5 hours. Decent quality magnetic charging cable provided. Use your own low power adapter, power bank or laptop.3) Has all the necessary health / workout tracking options.. Spo2( Oxymeter), Heart Rate monitor..Accuracy is 95-98%. Sleep tracking is pretty accurate too. Paedometer is accurate most of the times, but sometimes few hundred steps are added randomly without any activity. This happens randomly once in 3-4 days. Stress Monitor is also there but not sure how it's calculated. The sensors aren not fake most probably because if the watch isn't in contact with your skin it will display a warning message and won't display data.4) Lift to wake up gesture works but with a 1 second delay.. which is manageable. It has Tap to wake functionality too.5) Works with most popular notifications: Whatsapp, SMS, Facebook, Instagram etc. Can read the entire SMS on watch and most of the other messages unless it's very long.6) Calls can't be picked up or silenced.. You can only see the caller id and reject the call.7) BT Music Control, Weather ☁️ update and Alexa are other usable smart features.8) 50 different watch face are available on the Boat wave app. Some are really good.. You can also have customised wallpapers as watch faces . See the posted pictures.9) The Boat Wave app is neatly organized and syncs health data without any issues instantly. The app also has assisted GPS functionality which can track your running activities on a map, in case you need that data.10) The User Interface is smooth.. Please note that it's not laggy. The animations and transitions are a little slow but overall easy to use. Touch screen response is excellent and feels nice.11) Overall construction is sturdy and feels nice and comfortable to wear it. It has water resistance of 5 ATM.. Can take it for a short duration swim in a pool, under the shower or rain without any worries. Watch uppper body is brushed aluminium and under body is good quality plastic. The straps are soft and also of very good quality. It doesn't irritate your skin even after wearing it for long durations. Four colour options are available with equally matching straps.. Straps can be easily replaced with fancy straps.12 ) Works both with Android and iPhone flawlessly. Tested on both.TIPs AND TRICKs ________________________________________1) Boat wave app needs to run in the background all the time for your call notifications, message notifications, Alexa functionality and Weather updates. If you accidentally clear all the cache and background apps from the phone, the watch will disconnect from the phone after some time when idle ( no active inputs probably after 10-15 mins). Keep the boat wave app running in the background. Most people complaining that the watch frequently disconnected might unintentionally be clearing all the background apps. My watch was continuously connected for 4 straight days without me having to reconnect as long as the boat wave app was running in the background.2) Alexa on this watch can do a lot of things..It can set your alarms, start the stopwatch, show weather, control Alexa based devices like Echo, wireless lights and AC, work as a simple calculator, translate simple/ short English sentences to German, Spanish, Italian, French and Portugese, get you common stock quotes from internet, can you snippets of general information from the internet in case you don't know something. Yes, Alexa on your watch getting you the information is a little slow, takes about 30 -40 seconds to process your request but it's convenient and better that taking out the phone from your pocket which might take similar amount of time or longer. In my personal experience, Alexa works a little faster on Android as compared to iphone ( maybe 2-3 second difference). Also if there is break while speaking or if there is a long sentence, then it's difficult for Alexa to understand.. Check my video.. Keep it short and you should get the results accurately3) For Alexa to work properly: After connecting the Boat Wave app with an Amazon account, download the Alexa app and check your Xtend watch is visible under Devices option.4) To pickup and make calls handsfree without using the phone, just use a Bluetooth headset with voice assistant function. It will work as a charm. The speaker function on most smart watches is useless as it's not convenient for calls while traveling or in a crowded place due to low volume and obviously you don't want everyone to hear your private conversation.. With voice assistant feature on your BT headset you can make a call or play music without having to touch your phone.Few other functions which could have been provided and is missing. Actually available in many similarly priced devices :1) Torch 🔦 - Makes the display bright white.. Comes handy in darkness.2) Remote shutter button for camera.3) Call silencing option could have been added.

review_text: Extremely disappointing. Think twice before buyingThe software quality of this smartwatch is utterly unacceptable. Even if I receive a brand-new unit, I’m likely to face the exact same software issues.My biggest concern is the return policy. Products like smartwatches should have at least a 3-day return window, preferably around 10 days, so customers can properly test the device. What happens if someone receives a defective unit, gets it replaced, and the replacement is also defective? Are customers expected to keep going through service centres instead of simply being allowed to return the product?This is a basic electronic device that should work properly out of the box. Constantly resetting settings, the screen turning off, app connectivity problems, and poor software stability are simply not acceptable.My advice: Only consider buying this if you have a proper return window and enough time to thoroughly test it. Otherwise, you may end up stuck with a product that doesn’t work as expected.Very disappointed with the product and with the overall customer experience. Amazon should seriously reconsider the return policy for products like this.

review_title: iQOO 15R Review: Great Specs Ruined by Vulnerable Build & Exorbitant Repair Costs
review_text: ### **Summary of Key Customer Takeaways*** **Price & Value Proposition*** **Retail Price:** ~₹50,000.* **Underlying Risk:** Top-tier specs (Snapdragon 8 Gen 5, 144Hz AMOLED screen, 7,600mAh battery) are overshadowed by serious durability and after-sales issues.* **Water Resistance & Build Flaws*** **False Sense of Security:** Despite advertised IP ratings, ingress sealing is unreliable in real-world conditions.* **Moisture Susceptibility:** Minor exposure to light rain or everyday condensation leads to internal moisture, lens fogging, and hardware damage.* **Warranty & Repair Traps*** **No Warranty Coverage:** Standard manufacturer warranty strictly **excludes** liquid and moisture damage, leaving customers unprotected when sealing fails.* **Absurd Repair Costs:** Service centers quote repair bills around **₹40,000** (~80% of the phone's price), making repair practically unviable.* **Mandatory Hidden Overhead*** **Forced Insurance:** To safely use the phone outdoors, buying third-party insurance (~₹2,000+) is virtually mandatory.### **Bottom Line**A ₹50,000 investment turns into a useless device after a light rain, leaving you facing a ₹40,000 repair bill unless you pay extra upfront for insurance.

review_title: Misleading Product Information – Be Careful Before Buying for Wireless Charging!
review_text: I purchased this Ambrane power bank specifically for wireless charging, believing it would work as advertised. The product listing states that it supports iPhone 12 and above, but nowhere does it clearly mention that it only supports the older Qi wireless charging standard and not the newer Qi2 standard used by the latest iPhones (like iPhone 15).The Issue:• If you are buying this for wired charging, it works fine. No complaints there.• However, if you are planning to use wireless charging, be aware that it does NOT support full-speed 15W wireless charging on newer iPhones that use Qi2. Instead, you’ll only get 10W charging, not the advertised 15W.• This critical detail about Qi vs. Qi2 was not clearly mentioned on the product page, leading to confusion.Customer Support Experience:After realizing the issue, I contacted Ambrane’s customer support. Instead of acknowledging the lack of clear information in their listing, they simply told me that the problem is due to my iPhone running iOS 18 and using Qi2 wireless charging. This is misleading because it has nothing to do with iOS but rather with their power bank’s outdated charging standard.Additionally, I had to spend ₹340 just to ship the product to their service center, only for them to send it right back to me without a proper resolution. review_text: I’m a bit of a OnePlus loyalist. Ever since I got my first 7T back in January 2020, I haven't even looked at another brand. review_title: Bought It for 45K and Still Think It Was a Great Deal
review_text: I have been using the OnePlus 15R ACE version for a while now and overall I am quite happy with the purchase.CameraThe pundits are actually right on this one. The camera is probably the weakest point of the phone. I never cared that much about cameras though as I generally do not take too many photos. But the one time you pull out your phone for a special picture, that is when you feel that you are working with an average camera rather than something exceptional.That being said, I honestly do not mind the trade off. It is not as bad as some people make it sound. Most of the time it gets the job done and for my usage I am perfectly fine with it.BatteryI would say I am a moderate user. I do not charge it above 85 percent and I usually do not let it go below 15 percent either. Even with that habit, the phone comfortably lasts me more than a day.Charging is also pretty fast which is always a nice addition. Certain apps can drain the battery faster than expected, so I keep an app around to monitor these activities and keep things in check. Overall, I think this is more than a decent battery for this price range and the chip is using it very efficiently.PerformanceFor my usage the phone feels very snappy. One thing I like is that I do not have to sacrifice features thinking they might drain the battery. I keep everything turned up, high refresh rate and all the other settings at maximum.My usage is mostly on the productive side with some light gaming, the usual doomscrolling and everyday tasks. For all of that it has been excellent. It never feels like the device needs extra juice to get something done.ValueNow this is the biggest thing for me. I bought the ACE version for around 45k back in January and at that price this was an incredible value proposition. Seeing it now priced at 60k or even more honestly breaks my heart a little because that was a big part of what made this phone so attractive.Even then, I would still say it is a great purchase. When I compare it to the OnePlus 15 which is sitting around 90k right now, it honestly blows my mind. The OnePlus 15 is definitely the better phone, but the 15R gives you so much for the money that it still feels like a worthy purchase.Overall, I am very happy with the phone. The camera is average, the battery is excellent, the performance is smooth and reliable, and at the right price it is one of the best value purchases I have made in a long time.

review_text: This mobile's camera quality, picture quality when watching online videos, and overall system speed are inferior to the IQOO NEO 6 5G. This phone only has a nominal AI system; the AI ​​is completely non-functional 99% of the time. This phone also has significantly fewer functions and sub-functions in the settings and other folders compared to the IQOO NEO 6 5G. Flipkart, Amazon, and OnePlus apps and websites do not mention anywhere in the specifications that this phone has an ultrasonic fingerprint sensor. We only discovered it had an ultrasonic fingerprint sensor after the fingerprint sensor stopped working after installing a strong tempered glass screen protector. While ultrasonic fingerprint sensors might be good for security, they are not durable in terms of display protection. Only a thin, film-like screen protector works with this display. Even if you get the most expensive tempered glass from any shop or service center, this thin film or the tempered glass designed for the ultrasonic fingerprint sensor cannot protect the display, and there's a 100% chance the display will break if the phone is dropped. You either have to disable the fingerprint sensor by installing a strong tempered glass screen protector to protect the display, or take the risk of a broken display by using the thin, film-like tempered glass compatible with the ultrasonic fingerprint sensor. If we had known this beforehand, we would never have bought a phone with an ultrasonic fingerprint sensor.

review_title: Not bad, but definitely could be better! Are you listening, BOAT?
review_text: UPDATE: I'M CHANGING THE REVIEW FROM 1 TO 4. One of the rare moments where my initial disappointment led to a highly negative review but after using it (perforce!) for a few months, I feel differently.Don't get me wrong! The loud irritating "Bluetooth Mode", "Disconnected" announcements are still as irritating. The random disconnections don't seem random any more - Basically if you leave the bar connected for a long time without playing anything, and then afterwards you start playing something, it plays the music for some time, but then gets disconnected!Also, I've since discovered that the speakers in the bar ARE stereo (not mono as I'd thought) and play stereo audio well. Battery life is pretty good at around 4-5 hours I guess (I've never timed it!). The product is decently usable,Overall, not the best audio product I've owned (that too from Boat) but decent enough not to character assassinate!OLD REVIEW==========I genuinely cannot believe this product made it past Boat’s own internal quality checks. The Boat Avante Bar 490 is, without exaggeration, one of the most irritating and poorly designed audio devices I’ve ever used.First, the startup and shutdown experience is laughably bad. The thing screams “Bluetooth Mode” at full blast like it's trying to alert the entire neighborhood. No exaggeration, it’s jarring, obnoxious, and completely unnecessary. And before anyone asks, no, you cannot turn this dreadful voice off. Not through the device, not through the app, nowhere. It’s baked into the misery.Then there's the volume control, or rather the illusion of it. Press the volume buttons and you’re rewarded with a piercing beep that is somehow even louder than the startup voice. Does the volume actually change? Sometimes. Sometimes not. In my case, the volume didn’t decrease at all, but the beep made sure everyone in my house knew I tried. If you plan to adjust volume at night, don’t bother. You’ll end up waking everyone.Sound quality? Another disappointment. Most of the audio seems to come from the right side of this unusually long soundbar. If this is actually a single-speaker unit masquerading as a stereo soundbar, then the design borders on misleading. Why build something this wide if it’s going to output sound like a lopsided toy speaker?And of course, the Bluetooth connection. It randomly disconnects. Sometimes after a few minutes, sometimes whenever it feels like ruining your moment. And the disconnection announcement? Yet another ear-splitting shout. At this point, it’s almost comedic how consistently annoying this device is.Overall, this is a shockingly low-quality product from a brand I previously trusted. I’ve owned Boat Airdopes and the Stone 200 and have been quite happy with both. This, however, is a complete letdown. Easily the worst Boat product I’ve ever used.But the real punch in the gut is Amazon’s return policy. Unlike my other purchases, this piece of junk cannot be returned. Only replaced. Meaning I can exchange it for... another copy of the same loud, defective, headache-inducing soundbar. Amazing. Slow claps all around.If you value your ears, your peace, and your sanity, avoid the Boat Avante Bar 490. It’s a masterclass in bad design, bad execution, and bad user experience.

review_title: Tv is good, but only there service failed and fake promises.
review_text: Decent Display, But Service Falls ShortI bought the VW Spectra Series 43" QLED Android TV (VW43AQ3) a few weeks ago, and I have mixed feelings about it.Picture & Performance: The QLED panel delivers vibrant colors and sharp detail for a Full HD display, and the Android TV interface makes streaming apps like Netflix, YouTube, and Prime Video smooth and easy to navigate. For everyday viewing and casual gaming, it performs well and looks great in a mid-size room.Where It Falls Short: My biggest disappointment is with the after-sales service. There is no installation support included with the purchase. When I contacted customer care to ask for help mounting the TV, I was simply told to install it myself, entirely at my own risk — no technician visit, no guidance, nothing. For a TV in this price range, that's a significant gap.On top of that, when I tried reaching out about warranty and guarantee-related concerns, the only channel available was email, and responses were slow and unhelpful. There was no clear support number or live assistance to fall back on, which made the whole process frustrating.Verdict: Good hardware, disappointing support. If you're comfortable installing the TV yourself and don't mind relying solely on email for any warranty issues, it's a solid budget pick. But if you expect proper installation help or responsive customer service, be prepared for some frustration.

review_text: I purchased this TV today, 12/08/2026. At the time of delivery, a box-opening inspection was carried out. However, the TV was not switched on or tested. The delivery team told us that we could switch it on and check it later.After switching on the TV, we noticed clearly visible bright spots/light patches on the corners of the screen, particularly when displaying a black screen. This indicates a possible screen/backlight issue.We immediately reported the issue and requested a return. However, we were informed that there is no option for return because the box-opening inspection had already been completed.My question is: How can the TV's display quality or functionality be checked without actually switching it on? A box-opening inspection can only confirm the physical condition of the product and packaging. It cannot identify display defects that become visible only after the TV is powered on.Since the TV was purchased today, I request that you please reconsider the return/replacement and resolve this issue at the earliest.⚠️ Friends, please be carefulIf you are planning to purchase a TV, do not rely only on the box-opening inspection at the time of delivery. Ask the delivery team to switch on the TV and verify the display, especially for any bright spots, lines, patches, or other screen defects, before accepting the product.Please don't assume that a box-opening inspection means the TV has been properly tested.

review_title: Return Request Due to Unsatisfactory Quality and Undisclosed Self-Shipping Return Policy.
review_text: I purchased this bag because I found it suitable at the time of purchase. However, after receiving and examining the product, I found the quality to be only average and not satisfactory for my intended use. The bag is not necessarily defective or damaged, but I simply do not wish to keep or use it because I am not satisfied with its quality. I therefore decided to return it. However, I am unable to return the product because the self-shipment return policy being applied to my order was not clearly disclosed to me at the time of purchase. Had this condition been clearly communicated before placing the order, I would have been able to make an informed decision about purchasing the product. on my previous experience with Amazon, I expected that if I needed to return an item, the return would normally be picked up from my doorstep.However, when I decided to return I was surprised to see that Amazon was offering “I'll Send & Pay” instead of doorstep pickup. This means I have to pack the item, arrange and pay for the courier/India Post myself, and wait for Amazon to receive the parcel before the refund is processed.My main concern is that I was not clearly informed at the time of placing the order that the return would require self-shipping. If this information had been clearly shown before purchase, I could have considered it before ordering.I have been returning Amazon orders for years and have previously received doorstep return pickup, so this was an unexpected change for me.I am sharing this review so that other customers are aware that a returnable Amazon item may not necessarily have doorstep pickup and that they should check the return conditions carefully before purchasing, especially if self-shipping would be difficult or costly.I hope Amazon makes the return method and any self-shipping requirement clearly visible before customers place the order.

I called Amazon customer care and told them the number doesn’t work. They gave me another number and an email ID. The number also didn’t work and the email has been ignored completely – not even a basic reply.I called again. They lied and said my return window was extended and I just had to wait. I called again later – another lie – they told me they’d raised the issue for me and Seagate would respond. Still NOTHING.One customer service agent had the audacity to say I should submit the product to a Seagate service centre myself – which doesn’t even exist in my city! That’s right – they expect the customer to waste their own time, money, and effort for a defective product.Every customer care representative gave me different stories, all full of lies. Today is 28th June and I still have NO solution, NO return, and NO clarity. I’m stuck with a useless piece of junk and the worst customer service I’ve ever dealt with.This entire experience has been frustrating, infuriating, and insulting. Do yourself a favor – DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT. DO NOT TRUST THE SUPPORT. Once you buy it, you’re on your own.
